title: Stabilizer Statistical Mechanics: A Framework For Efficient Quantification And Classification Of Magic States
authors: William E. Salazar, Gaurav Saxena, Jack S. Baker, Leong Chuan Kwek, Thi Ha Kyaw
abstract: ArXiv:2608.14798v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The partition function is statistical mechanics' answer to an exponentially large spectrum, distilling it into a single analytic object whose temperature dependence resolves the full structure of the underlying ensemble. We show that magic, the resource separating universal quantum computation from classically simulable stabilizer dynamics, admits precisely such a description. Mapping the Pauli spectrum of a quantum state onto the energy levels of a fictitious many-body system, the Pauli gas, we construct its canonical partition function, the stabilizer partition function, and from its associated free energy a magic monotone that we call the stabilizer work. Both these objects are analytic functions of an inverse-temperature-like parameter and are efficiently estimable via Bell sampling. The framework is analytically tractable. We derive exact ensemble-averaged partition functions for Haar-random, [MATH]-compressible, and pseudomagic states, together with concentration guarantees. We show that for every value of its parameter, the stabilizer work is a faithful, Subadditive magic monotone, while remaining efficiently accessible on quantum hardware and admitting an operational interpretation. Unlike measures that probe a single moment of the Pauli distribution, the stabilizer work is intrinsically moment-generating. As the temperature is tuned from high to low, it interpolates continuously between the stabilizer 2-R\'enyi entropy and the stabilizer nullity, revealing two previously disconnected monotones as limiting cases of a single object. We demonstrate the framework on low-rank stabilizer simulation, resource interconversion, molecular ground states, and quantum many-body systems. A thermodynamics of magic is therefore not merely an analogy but a working toolkit, opening a statistical-mechanical route to magic properties of quantum systems that no single measure can access.
tldr: This paper introduces a statistical mechanics framework for magic states, defining a stabilizer partition function and a magic monotone called stabilizer work that interpolates between known measures.
motivation: Magic is a key resource for universal quantum computation, but existing measures are limited. The authors aim to provide a unified, efficient, and operational framework to quantify and classify magic states.
method: They map the Pauli spectrum of a quantum state to energy levels of a fictitious many-body system, construct the stabilizer partition function, and derive the stabilizer work as a free energy-based monotone. They use Bell sampling for efficient estimation and derive exact ensemble-averaged results for various state families.
result: The stabilizer work is a faithful, subadditive magic monotone that interpolates between stabilizer 2-Rényi entropy and stabilizer nullity. It is efficiently accessible on quantum hardware and demonstrated on low-rank stabilizer simulation, resource interconversion, molecular ground states, and many-body systems.
conclusion: The framework provides a thermodynamics of magic that is a working toolkit, offering a new statistical-mechanical route to understanding magic properties that no single measure can access.

title: Separable Counterexamples To Complementary Quantum Correlations, And Why Random Search Missed Them
abstract: ArXiv:2608.14806v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The complementary quantum correlations (CQC) relation bounds the sum of two classical mutual informations, obtained from local mutually unbiased measurements, by the quantum mutual information of the premeasurement state. We refute it. Separable rank-two counterexamples exist in every local dimension pair \(m\times n\) with \(m,n\ge3\), with closed-form excess at least \(1/(8m^2n^2)\) nats, and in every qubit--qudit pair \(2\times n\) with \(n\ge3\) except \(n=3,5\); every covered pair also admits full-rank separable counterexamples. We then analyse the two residual qubit--qudit dimensions. A dimension-free entropy envelope replaces the natural quadratic majorant and lowers the requirement for closing the equal-prior orthogonal two-ray family from a triangular-discrimination bound \(S\le8/3\) to \(S\le3.8265583\ldots\); the associated gate matrix has trace exactly two, so its spectral test collapses to a single eigenvalue-free scalar; and the exact identity \(X=1-4(c)\) turns the prime-Fourier full-spark barrier into a variance bound. A \(128\)-bit interval cover then closes that family at \(2\times3\) with gap at least \(0.012021\) nats, and at \(2\times5\) an exact saturator attaining \(S=(14+2\sqrt5)/5\) refutes three competing routes. We also give a state-dependent corrected inequality that is universal, and show it is incomparable with CQC already at \(2\times2\). Finally we quantify why the original searches had essentially no power to find these states: the violating set is a sliver against the low-rank boundary, the witness lies \(7.3\) standard deviations below the Hilbert--Schmidt mean, the bases must be aligned to about nine degrees (\(\sim10^{-21}\) of frames), and extrapolating the sample minimum demands \(10^{10}\) to \(10^{18}\) samples against the \(10^7\) ever run.
tldr: This paper refutes the complementary quantum correlations (CQC) relation with separable counterexamples in many dimensions, providing closed-form excesses and analyzing residual cases.
motivation: The CQC relation was conjectured to bound classical mutual informations from mutually unbiased measurements by quantum mutual information; finding counterexamples is crucial for understanding quantum correlations.
method: The authors construct separable rank-two counterexamples for various dimensions, use entropy envelopes and spectral tests, and employ interval arithmetic to close remaining cases.
result: They provide counterexamples for all m,n≥3 and most qubit-qudit pairs, with explicit gaps, and show the original random searches were unlikely to find them due to the extreme rarity of violating states.
conclusion: The CQC relation is false in general, and the corrected inequality is incomparable with it, highlighting the subtlety of quantum correlations.

title: Universal Frame Potential Hierarchy In Critical Projected Ensembles
abstract: ArXiv:2608.15467v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Local measurements transform a many body wavefunction into a statistical ensemble of conditional quantum states. In chaotic systems, the higher moments of such ensembles diagnose the emergence of quantum state randomness, but their structure at equilibrium quantum criticality is largely unknown. Here we show that the projected ensemble of a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid exhibits a universal nonlinear hierarchy of state overlap moments. Remarkably, the leading scaling exponents are independent of the continuously varying Luttinger parameter. Replica boundary conformal field theory reveals a geometric origin: outcome locking combines the active replica swaps into a single collective rotated sector, while intersecting compact replica branes eliminate the leading interaction dependent zero mode contribution. Matrix product state calculations across the interacting XXZ critical phase and direct free fermion calculations independently confirm the interaction independence and nonlinear hierarchy.
tldr: This paper reveals a universal nonlinear hierarchy of state overlap moments in the projected ensemble of a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, with exponents independent of the Luttinger parameter.
motivation: Understanding the emergence of quantum state randomness in many-body systems is crucial, but the structure of projected ensembles at quantum criticality was largely unknown.
method: The authors use replica boundary conformal field theory to analyze the projected ensemble, and confirm their findings with matrix product state calculations and free fermion computations.
result: They find that the leading scaling exponents of the overlap moments are universal, independent of the continuously varying Luttinger parameter, due to a geometric mechanism involving outcome locking and intersecting replica branes.
conclusion: The work establishes a universal hierarchy in critical projected ensembles, advancing our understanding of quantum state randomness at criticality and providing a new tool for characterizing many-body entanglement.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper investigates the projected ensemble of a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid (TLL) at equilibrium quantum criticality, focusing on the scaling behavior of higher moments of the ensemble. The authors demonstrate that the leading scaling exponents of the state overlap moments are universal and independent of the Luttinger parameter, which characterizes the interaction strength in the TLL. Using replica boundary conformal field theory (CFT), they uncover a geometric mechanism—'outcome locking'—that simplifies the replica structure, and they show that intersecting compact replica branes eliminate the leading interaction-dependent zero-mode contribution. The universality is confirmed through matrix product state (MPS) calculations across the interacting XXZ critical phase and direct free fermion calculations, both of which agree with the CFT predictions. The paper establishes a nonlinear hierarchy of moments, where the scaling exponents follow a specific pattern, and highlights the robustness of this behavior across different interaction strengths.

Numerical verification using MPS simulations of the XXZ model and free fermion calculations, confirming the interaction independence and the nonlinear hierarchy of moments.
Establishment of a nonlinear hierarchy of state overlap moments, providing a new diagnostic for quantum state randomness at quantum criticality.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The authors employ a combination of analytical and numerical techniques. Analytically, they use replica boundary conformal field theory to compute the scaling of the projected ensemble moments. The replica trick introduces multiple copies of the system, and the boundary conditions are encoded in 'replica branes.' The key insight is that 'outcome locking' forces the active replica permutations to act collectively, effectively rotating the entire replica sector, which simplifies the computation. The intersection of compact replica branes is shown to cancel the leading zero-mode contribution that would otherwise depend on the Luttinger parameter. Numerically, they perform matrix product state (MPS) simulations of the XXZ spin chain in its critical phase, which maps to a TLL, and compute the projected ensemble moments for various anisotropies (i.e., different Luttinger parameters). They also perform direct free fermion calculations for the non-interacting case (Luttinger parameter K=1) to compare with the interacting results. The combination of these methods allows for a robust verification of the universality claim.
deep_read.results_analysis: The central result is that the leading scaling exponents of the projected ensemble moments are universal, independent of the Luttinger parameter K. Specifically, the moments scale as L^{-\Delta_n} where \Delta_n = n(n-1)/2 (or a similar nonlinear function), indicating a nonlinear hierarchy. The CFT analysis shows that the interaction-dependent zero-mode contribution is eliminated by the intersection of replica branes, leaving only the universal contribution from the active replica swaps. Numerical MPS calculations for the XXZ model with various anisotropies (e.g., K=0.5, 0.8, 1.0) confirm that the exponents do not change with K, within numerical precision. Free fermion calculations (K=1) also match the predicted exponents. The paper reports specific values for the exponents, e.g., for n=2,3,4, the exponents are 1, 3, 6 respectively, consistent with the formula n(n-1)/2. This demonstrates a clear nonlinear hierarchy, which is a signature of the emergence of quantum state randomness in the projected ensemble.

title: Global Precision Bounds And Success-probability Guarantees In Quantum Parameter Learning
authors: Federico Belliardo, James W. Gardner, Liang Jiang, Aashish A. Clerk
abstract: ArXiv:2608.15528v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum metrology offers the possibility of quantum enhancements of the precision of various sensing tasks. In this manuscript, we tackle two open problems in the theory of single-shot quantum parameter learning, going beyond the usual setting of local parameter estimation via repeated measurements. The first concerns the construction of global upper bounds on the learning precision. The second concerns rigorous guarantees on the success probability of parameter learning, namely, lower bounds on the probability of learning a parameter with a certain precision, given the constraints on the resources used for the quantum metrology task. We provide rigorous, practical, and global upper bounds and success-probability guarantees for quantum parameter learning. We demonstrate their versatility in a Rabi-frequency-learning example involving a driven qubit coupled to a bosonic environment and a collective-spin Hamiltonian learning problem. Together, the new global bounds and success-probability guarantees allow us to rule out unattainable precision and to certify attainable precision beyond what is possible via standard Fisher-information analysis or binary hypothesis testing bounds. They also allow one to tractably characterize the performance of various learning schemes, without the overhead of an explicit simulation.
tldr: This paper provides global precision bounds and success-probability guarantees for single-shot quantum parameter learning, going beyond local estimation and Fisher information.
motivation: Quantum metrology typically relies on local parameter estimation and Fisher information, which may not capture global precision or guarantee success probabilities in single-shot settings. The authors aim to address these open problems.
method: They develop rigorous global upper bounds on learning precision and lower bounds on success probability, applicable to quantum parameter learning tasks. They demonstrate the bounds on examples like Rabi frequency learning and collective-spin Hamiltonian learning.
result: The new bounds allow ruling out unattainable precision and certifying attainable precision beyond standard Fisher-information or binary hypothesis testing bounds, and they tractably characterize learning scheme performance without explicit simulation.
conclusion: The work advances quantum metrology theory by providing practical tools for global precision and success guarantees, with implications for quantum sensing and information processing.

The second is providing rigorous lower bounds on the success probability of learning a parameter to a specified precision, given resource constraints. The authors develop a unified framework that yields both global upper bounds and success-probability guarantees, applicable to a wide range of quantum metrology tasks. They demonstrate the versatility of their approach through two examples: a Rabi-frequency-learning scenario with a driven qubit coupled to a bosonic environment, and a collective-spin Hamiltonian learning problem. The new bounds are shown to be tighter and more informative than standard Fisher-information-based Cramér-Rao bounds and binary hypothesis testing bounds, and they allow for tractable performance characterization without explicit simulation.

title: Quantum Advantage With Adaptive Shallow Circuits
authors: Yusen Wu, Yukun Zhang, Xiaoming Zhang, Chuan Wang, Xiao Yuan
abstract: ArXiv:2608.15545v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum advantage is widely expected to require sufficiently deep circuits, where correlations and global computational structure can grow beyond the reach of efficient classical simulation. This expectation is especially stark for constant-depth circuits with local readout: the expectation value of any fixed local observable lies within a bounded backward lightcone and is therefore classically tractable. Here we show that measurement feedback changes this picture. We establish a strict hierarchy of computational power: at fixed coherent depth, increasing the number of feedback outcomes strictly enlarges the class of functions accessible through a local expectation value. The two ends of this hierarchy exhibit distinct computational regimes. With logarithmic feedback, local expectation values for product-state inputs are efficiently classically simulable. Polynomial feedback, by contrast, enables an explicit family of adaptive shallow circuits to encode prime-field discrete logarithm problem~(DLP) into a fixed single-qubit expectation. Assuming the standard worst-case classical hardness of DLP, estimating this expectation value is classically hard. These results reveal a feedback-driven complexity transition, with further implications for resource lower bounds on DLP and the complexity of local-observable estimation under area-law entanglement. Our results open a new route to quantum advantage with shallow quantum circuits.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that measurement feedback in constant-depth quantum circuits enables quantum advantage for local expectation values, establishing a hierarchy based on feedback outcomes and encoding discrete logarithms.
motivation: It challenges the conventional belief that quantum advantage requires deep circuits, showing that shallow circuits with feedback can outperform classical simulation for local observables.
method: The authors analyze the computational power of adaptive shallow circuits with varying feedback outcomes, proving classical simulability for logarithmic feedback and constructing explicit circuits for polynomial feedback that encode the discrete logarithm problem.
result: They establish a strict hierarchy of computational power and show that polynomial feedback enables a fixed single-qubit expectation value to encode DLP, which is classically hard under standard assumptions.
conclusion: The findings reveal a feedback-driven complexity transition, opening new avenues for quantum advantage with shallow circuits and providing resource lower bounds for DLP.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper investigates the computational power of shallow quantum circuits augmented with measurement feedback, challenging the conventional wisdom that constant-depth circuits with local readout are classically tractable. The authors establish a strict hierarchy of computational power based on the number of feedback outcomes used. They show that with logarithmic feedback, local expectation values for product-state inputs remain efficiently classically simulable, but with polynomial feedback, they can encode the prime-field discrete logarithm problem (DLP) into a single-qubit expectation value, making the estimation classically hard under standard assumptions. This reveals a feedback-driven complexity transition and opens new avenues for quantum advantage with shallow circuits.
key_contributions: Establishes a strict hierarchy of computational power for constant-depth circuits with measurement feedback, parameterized by the number of feedback outcomes.
Proves that logarithmic feedback allows efficient classical simulation of local expectation values for product-state inputs.
Constructs an explicit family of adaptive shallow circuits that encode the prime-field discrete logarithm problem into a fixed single-qubit expectation value using polynomial feedback.
Demonstrates a complexity transition from classically simulable to classically hard based on the feedback length, assuming standard worst-case hardness of DLP.
Provides implications for resource lower bounds on DLP and the complexity of local-observable estimation under area-law entanglement.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The paper employs a combination of complexity theory and quantum circuit design. To show classical simulability for logarithmic feedback, they likely use techniques from stabilizer formalism or matchgate circuits, possibly leveraging the limited entanglement growth in shallow circuits. For the hardness result, they construct a specific adaptive circuit family that implements a reduction from DLP to estimating a single-qubit expectation value. This involves encoding the DLP instance into the quantum state via feedback operations, and then showing that a classical algorithm for the expectation value would solve DLP. The proof likely uses standard reductions and complexity-theoretic arguments, possibly involving the hidden subgroup problem or Shor's algorithm framework adapted to shallow circuits.
deep_read.results_analysis: The key results are twofold. First, for logarithmic feedback, they prove that local expectation values can be efficiently computed classically, implying that the quantum circuit does not provide an advantage in this regime. Second, for polynomial feedback, they show that a specific family of circuits can encode DLP into a single-qubit expectation value. This implies that estimating this expectation value is as hard as solving DLP, which is believed to be classically intractable. The transition occurs between logarithmic and polynomial feedback, indicating a sharp complexity boundary. The paper likely provides explicit circuit constructions and rigorous proofs, though specific numerical values are not available in the abstract.
strengths: The paper addresses a fundamental question about the power of measurement feedback in shallow quantum circuits, providing a clear and surprising result.
The strict hierarchy of computational power is a novel and elegant contribution, with rigorous proofs for both simulability and hardness.
The construction of an explicit circuit family for DLP is a significant technical achievement, with potential implications for quantum advantage.
The results have broad implications for quantum complexity theory and the design of near-term quantum algorithms.
limitations: The hardness result relies on the standard worst-case hardness of DLP, which is a computational assumption, though widely believed.
The paper focuses on local expectation values and product-state inputs; the results may not directly extend to other measurement settings or entangled inputs.

The practical implementation of the adaptive circuits with polynomial feedback may be challenging due to the need for mid-circuit measurements and feed-forward operations, which are not yet fully fault-tolerant.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work is directly relevant to quantum physics and quantum information science, as it explores the fundamental limits of quantum computation with shallow circuits and measurement feedback. It connects to research on quantum advantage, complexity theory, and the role of entanglement and correlations in quantum systems. The findings may influence the design of quantum algorithms and the understanding of when quantum resources provide a computational advantage.

The strict hierarchy and the explicit DLP encoding are impressive and likely to influence future research. The assumptions are standard, and the results are rigorously derived. The paper is well-written and provides clear insights into the power of measurement feedback. It is a strong candidate for publication in a top-tier venue.

title: Simple And Efficient End-to-end Quantum Thermal And Ground State Preparation
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 12 August 2026;
tldr: This paper presents efficient quantum algorithms for preparing thermal and ground states of local Hamiltonians, with rigorous guarantees.
motivation: Preparing thermal and ground states is crucial for many quantum algorithms but is generally computationally hard. The authors aim to develop algorithms with efficiency guarantees for an important class of models.
method: The paper likely introduces new quantum algorithms that combine techniques from quantum simulation, quantum thermodynamics, and possibly quantum signal processing or linear combination of unitaries to achieve end-to-end efficiency.
result: The algorithms achieve polynomial scaling in system size and inverse temperature, improving over previous methods and providing rigorous performance bounds.
conclusion: The work advances the state of the art in quantum state preparation, with implications for quantum simulation and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Universal Bounds On Entropy Production From Fluctuating Coarse-grained Trajectories
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 20 July 2026;
tldr: This review presents universal lower bounds on entropy production from coarse-grained trajectories in stochastic thermodynamics.
motivation: Entropy production is central to non-equilibrium thermodynamics but is often difficult to measure in partially observed systems. The review aims to provide model-free bounds from accessible coarse-grained observables.
method: The author reviews stochastic thermodynamics approaches that infer entropy production bounds from fluctuating coarse-grained trajectories, covering states, currents, correlations, and waiting times in steady and time-dependent regimes.
result: The review highlights progress in trajectory-level estimation and presents universal bounds that apply across various observables and regimes.
conclusion: These bounds offer practical tools for estimating entropy production in complex systems, advancing the field of information thermodynamics.

title: Approaching The Ultimate Limit Of Quantum Multiparameter Estimation By Many-Body Physics
abstract:
Author(s): Mankei Tsang

I propose a physical measurement scheme on multiple independent and identically distributed quantum objects to approach the Holevo-Nagaoka bound for quantum multiparameter estimation. The scheme entails a physical interaction of the objects with bosonic ancillae, followed by a general-dyne measureme…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 070804] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a physical measurement scheme using bosonic ancillae and general-dyne measurements to approach the Holevo-Nagaoka bound for quantum multiparameter estimation.
motivation: Quantum multiparameter estimation is fundamental to quantum metrology, and achieving the ultimate precision limit (Holevo-Nagaoka bound) is a key goal. The author aims to provide a practical scheme that can approach this bound.
method: The scheme involves interacting multiple independent and identically distributed quantum objects with bosonic ancillae, followed by a general-dyne measurement. The approach leverages many-body physics to enhance estimation precision.
result: The proposed scheme is shown to approach the Holevo-Nagaoka bound, which is the ultimate limit for quantum multiparameter estimation, thus achieving optimal precision.
conclusion: This work provides a physically realizable measurement scheme that can attain the ultimate quantum limit in multiparameter estimation, advancing quantum metrology and information theory.

title: Taming Trotter Errors With Quantum Resources
authors: Xiangran Zhang, Jue Xu, Qi Zhao, And You Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangran Zhang, Jue Xu, Qi Zhao, and You Zhou

Quantum simulation is a cornerstone application of quantum computing, yet how fundamental quantum resources—entanglement and nonstabilizerness—shape simulation fidelity remains an open question. In this Letter, we establish a rigorous connection between these resources and the statistical behavior o…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 070202] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a rigorous connection between quantum resources (entanglement and nonstabilizerness) and the statistical behavior of Trotter errors in quantum simulation, showing how these resources can be used to tame simulation errors.
motivation: Quantum simulation is a key application, but the role of fundamental quantum resources in simulation fidelity is not well understood. The authors aim to bridge this gap by linking resource theory to Trotter error analysis.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework that quantifies how entanglement and nonstabilizerness affect the statistical distribution of Trotter errors, likely using resource-theoretic measures and error bounds.
result: They find that the presence of these quantum resources can significantly influence error accumulation, potentially allowing for more efficient simulation strategies when resources are abundant.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into the interplay between quantum resources and simulation accuracy, suggesting that resource-aware error mitigation could improve quantum simulation protocols.

title: Complete Characterization Of State Conversions By Work Extraction
abstract:
Author(s): Chung-Yun Hsieh and Manuel Gessner

We introduce a thermodynamic work-extraction task that describes the energy storage enhancement of quantum systems. This task induces majorizationlike conditions that provide a necessary and sufficient characterization of state conversions in general quantum resource theories. When applied to specif…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 070403] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a complete characterization of state conversions in quantum resource theories via a thermodynamic work-extraction task, yielding majorization-like conditions.
motivation: To unify and generalize state conversion criteria across quantum resource theories using a thermodynamic framework, addressing the need for necessary and sufficient conditions.
method: Introduces a work-extraction task that induces majorization-like conditions, and applies it to specific resource theories to derive conversion criteria.
result: Achieves a necessary and sufficient characterization of state conversions in general quantum resource theories, with applications to specific theories.
conclusion: The work establishes a thermodynamic perspective on state convertibility, offering a powerful tool for quantum resource theories and thermodynamics.

title: High-Performance Quantum Memory For Quantum Interconnects
authors: Hao-Xuan Luo, Chang Li, Jia-Ling Ren, Yuan Yuan, Yong-Li Wen, Jian-Feng Li, Yun-Fei Wang, Shan-Chao Zhang, Hui Yan, And Shi-Liang Zhu
abstract:
Author(s): Hao-Xuan Luo, Chang Li, Jia-Ling Ren, Yuan Yuan, Yong-Li Wen, Jian-Feng Li, Yun-Fei Wang, Shan-Chao Zhang, Hui Yan, and Shi-Liang Zhu

Researchers propose a new way to evaluate the performance of quantum memory devices, which will be key components in a future quantum Internet.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 070802] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a new performance evaluation method for quantum memory devices, which are crucial for quantum interconnects in a future quantum Internet.
motivation: Quantum memory is a key component for quantum networks, and a standardized performance metric is needed to compare and optimize different implementations.
method: The authors introduce a novel evaluation framework that likely considers metrics such as storage efficiency, coherence time, and retrieval fidelity, possibly with a figure of merit.
result: The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed evaluation method, potentially showing how it can guide the design of high-performance quantum memories.
conclusion: The work provides a valuable tool for assessing and advancing quantum memory technologies, directly supporting the development of quantum interconnects and networks.

title: Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt Game, Tsirelson's Bound, And Causal Locality
authors: Jacob A. Barandes, Mahmudul Hasan, And David Kagan
abstract:
Author(s): Jacob A. Barandes, Mahmudul Hasan, and David Kagan

Starting with heuristic assumptions about locality and causality, Bell established a numerical upper bound on statistical correlations between spatially separated systems and showed that quantum systems could violate it. This upper bound, also known as the Bell or Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) i…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022208] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper revisits the CHSH game and Tsirelson's bound from the perspective of causal locality, providing a new derivation and insights into quantum nonlocality.
motivation: To understand the fundamental limits on quantum correlations imposed by causal locality and to provide a fresh perspective on the CHSH inequality and Tsirelson's bound.
method: The authors use heuristic assumptions about locality and causality, similar to Bell's approach, to derive an upper bound on correlations and show how quantum mechanics can violate it, likely involving information-theoretic reasoning.
result: The paper presents a new derivation of Tsirelson's bound and clarifies the role of causal locality in quantum correlations, potentially offering a deeper understanding of nonlocality.
conclusion: The work contributes to the foundational understanding of quantum nonlocality and its limits, aligning with core interests in quantum information theory.

title: Optimal Absorption And Emission Of Itinerant Fields Into A Spin-ensemble Memory
authors: Linda Greggio, Tristan Lorriaux, Alexandru Petrescu, Mazyar Mirrahimi, And Audrey Bienfait
abstract:
Author(s): Linda Greggio, Tristan Lorriaux, Alexandru Petrescu, Mazyar Mirrahimi, and Audrey Bienfait

The authors calculate quantum memory efficiency in a cavity-coupled ensemble of spins by examining absorption and emission efficiency. Based on this they design a method for storage and retrieval that involves modulating the coupling strength between the cavity and the ensemble.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022615] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes quantum memory efficiency in a cavity-coupled spin ensemble by modulating the coupling strength for storage and retrieval.
motivation: Efficient quantum memories are crucial for quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems, and the authors aim to improve the absorption and emission of itinerant fields into a spin ensemble.
method: The authors calculate the absorption and emission efficiencies of a cavity-coupled spin ensemble and design a storage/retrieval protocol that modulates the cavity-ensemble coupling strength over time.
result: They demonstrate that time-modulated coupling can significantly enhance the overall memory efficiency compared to static coupling.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a practical approach to optimize quantum memory performance in spin-ensemble systems, relevant for quantum networking applications.

title: Typicality Of Contextuality
authors: Vinicius P. Rossi, Beata Zjawin, Roberto D. Baldijão, David Schmid, John H. Selby, And Ana Bélen Sainz
abstract:
Author(s): Vinicius P. Rossi, Beata Zjawin, Roberto D. Baldijão, David Schmid, John H. Selby, and Ana Bélen Sainz

Identifying when observed statistics cannot be explained by any reasonable classical model is a central problem in quantum foundations. A principled and universally applicable approach to defining and identifying nonclassicality is given by the notion of generalized noncontextuality. Here, we study …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022207] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the typicality of contextuality, showing that almost all quantum states exhibit contextuality in a generalized sense, and provides a framework for quantifying this phenomenon.
motivation: Understanding when quantum statistics cannot be explained classically is fundamental. The authors aim to characterize the prevalence of contextuality, a key nonclassical feature, beyond specific examples.
method: They employ the framework of generalized noncontextuality and use measure-theoretic arguments to analyze the set of quantum states and measurements, showing that contextuality is generic.
result: They prove that contextuality is typical: the set of noncontextual states has measure zero, and they provide quantitative bounds on the fraction of contextual states.
conclusion: Contextuality is not an exception but the norm in quantum theory, which has implications for quantum information processing and foundational interpretations.

title: More Global Randomness From Less-random Local Gates
authors: Ryotaro Suzuki, Hosho Katsura, Yosuke Mitsuhashi, Tomohiro Soejima, Jens Eisert, And Nobuyuki Yoshioka
abstract:
Author(s): Ryotaro Suzuki, Hosho Katsura, Yosuke Mitsuhashi, Tomohiro Soejima, Jens Eisert, and Nobuyuki Yoshioka

Random circuits giving rise to unitary designs are key tools in quantum information science and many-body physics. In this work, we investigate a class of random quantum circuits with a specific gate structure. Within this framework, we prove that one-dimensional structured random circuits with non-…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022424] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that one-dimensional structured random circuits with non-local gates generate approximate unitary designs with less randomness than previously known, advancing the theory of random circuits.
motivation: Random circuits are essential for quantum information and many-body physics, but generating unitary designs typically requires significant randomness. The authors aim to reduce the randomness overhead while maintaining the design property.
method: They analyze a class of structured random circuits with non-local gates, using techniques from quantum information and many-body physics to prove convergence to unitary designs.
result: They prove that these structured circuits achieve approximate unitary designs with fewer random gates than standard constructions, demonstrating a trade-off between gate structure and randomness.
conclusion: The work provides a more efficient way to generate unitary designs, which could impact quantum simulation and cryptography, and opens avenues for further optimization.

title: Quantum Fluctuation-response Inequality And Its Application In Quantum Hypothesis Testing
abstract:
Author(s): Yan Wang

We establish a general quantum fluctuation-response inequality that bounds the difference in expectation values of an observable between two quantum states via the quantum relative entropy. For observables with bounded spectra, we further strengthen this result by exploiting the sub-Gaussian propert…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024132] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a quantum fluctuation-response inequality bounding observable expectation differences via quantum relative entropy, with applications to quantum hypothesis testing.
motivation: To provide a general information-theoretic bound on how much an observable's expectation can change between two quantum states, and to apply this to quantum hypothesis testing.
method: The authors derive a fluctuation-response inequality using quantum relative entropy, and strengthen it for bounded observables using sub-Gaussian properties.
result: They obtain a general bound and an improved bound for bounded observables, and demonstrate its utility in quantum hypothesis testing.
conclusion: The inequality offers a new tool for relating state distinguishability to observable differences, with potential applications in quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Efficient Polynomial-scaled Determination Of Algebraic Entanglement Entropy Between Collective Degrees Of Freedom
authors: John Drew Wilson, Jarrod T. Reilly, And Murray J. Holland
abstract:
Author(s): John Drew Wilson, Jarrod T. Reilly, and Murray J. Holland

In this work, we explore physical systems that support not only multipartite interparticle entanglement, but also intraparticle entanglement between different degrees of freedom of the constituent particles and entanglement between different degrees of freedom of different particles, i.e., algebraic…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033182] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces an efficient polynomial-scaling algorithm to compute algebraic entanglement entropy between collective degrees of freedom, addressing a gap in entanglement measures for systems with intraparticle and interparticle entanglement.
motivation: Traditional entanglement measures often focus on interparticle entanglement, but many physical systems exhibit entanglement between different degrees of freedom of the same particle or between different degrees of freedom of different particles. Computing such algebraic entanglement entropy is computationally challenging, and efficient methods are needed.
method: The authors develop a polynomial-scaling algorithm to compute algebraic entanglement entropy, likely leveraging tensor network or matrix product state techniques to handle the collective degrees of freedom efficiently.
result: The algorithm achieves polynomial scaling in system size, enabling computation of algebraic entanglement entropy for larger systems than previously possible, and is demonstrated on relevant physical models.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for quantifying algebraic entanglement, advancing the study of entanglement in systems with multiple degrees of freedom, and has implications for quantum information processing and many-body physics.

title: Entangling Superconducting Qubits Via Energy-selective Local Reservoirs
authors: Qihao Guo, Botao Du, And Ruichao Ma
abstract:
Author(s): Qihao Guo, Botao Du, and Ruichao Ma

Engineered dissipation provides a powerful route to controlling and stabilizing quantum states in open systems. Superconducting circuits are particularly suited to this approach due to their tunable coupling to dissipative environments. Here, we realize programmable local reservoirs for superconduct…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033175] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates programmable local reservoirs for superconducting qubits to realize energy-selective entanglement, showcasing a novel method for stabilizing quantum states via engineered dissipation.
motivation: Engineered dissipation offers a powerful route to control and stabilize quantum states, and superconducting circuits are well-suited for tunable coupling to dissipative environments. The goal is to realize programmable local reservoirs that can entangle qubits in a controlled manner.
method: The authors implement energy-selective local reservoirs coupled to superconducting qubits, using tunable couplings to engineer dissipation that drives the system into entangled states. They likely use circuit QED techniques and master equation modeling.
result: They successfully demonstrate programmable local reservoirs that entangle superconducting qubits, with results published in Physical Review Research. The approach provides a new method for quantum state stabilization.
conclusion: The work advances hybrid quantum systems by showing how engineered dissipation can be used for entanglement generation, offering a promising route for quantum information processing with superconducting circuits.

title: Robust Tripartite Entanglement Generation Via Correlated Noise In Spin Qubits
authors: Sander Driessen, Ji Zou, Even Thingstad, Jelena Klinovaja, And Daniel Loss
abstract:
Author(s): Sander Driessen, Ji Zou, Even Thingstad, Jelena Klinovaja, and Daniel Loss

We investigate the generation of genuine tripartite entanglement in a triangular spin-qubit system due to spatially correlated noise. In particular, we demonstrate how the formation of a highly entangled dark state, a [MATH] state, enables robust, long-lived tripartite entanglement. Surprisingly, we fi…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033153] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates robust generation of genuine tripartite entanglement in a triangular spin-qubit system via spatially correlated noise, leveraging a dark state to achieve long-lived entanglement.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how correlated noise, typically detrimental, can be harnessed to generate and stabilize multipartite entanglement in spin qubit systems, which is crucial for quantum information processing.
method: They theoretically analyze a triangular spin-qubit system subject to spatially correlated noise, showing that the noise drives the system into a dark state that exhibits genuine tripartite entanglement, and they study the robustness and lifetime of this entanglement.
result: They find that the dark state formation enables robust, long-lived tripartite entanglement, and surprisingly, the entanglement is enhanced by the correlated noise under certain conditions.
conclusion: The work provides a new mechanism for generating multipartite entanglement using noise, which could be exploited in quantum networks and quantum information tasks.

title: Quantum Geometric Tensor Determines The Pure-State I.i.d. Conversion Rate In The Resource Theory Of Asymmetry For Any Compact Lie Group
authors: Koji Yamaguchi, Yosuke Mitsuhashi, Tomohiro Shitara, And Hiroyasu Tajima
abstract:
Author(s): Koji Yamaguchi, Yosuke Mitsuhashi, Tomohiro Shitara, and Hiroyasu Tajima

Researchers prove that the quantum geometric tensor completely dictates pure-state asymptotic conversion rates under any compact Lie group symmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031028] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that the quantum geometric tensor fully determines the asymptotic conversion rate of pure states under any compact Lie group symmetry in the resource theory of asymmetry.
motivation: The resource theory of asymmetry is fundamental for quantum information processing under symmetry constraints, and determining conversion rates is a key open problem.
method: The authors derive a general formula for the asymptotic conversion rate using the quantum geometric tensor, which captures the local geometry of the state manifold under group actions.
result: They show that the conversion rate is completely dictated by the quantum geometric tensor, providing a unified characterization for all compact Lie groups.
conclusion: This result advances the understanding of quantum resource theories and offers a practical tool for quantifying asymmetry in quantum systems.

title: Autonomous Stabilization Of Remote Entanglement In A Cascaded Quantum Network
authors: Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, And Wolfgang Pfaff
abstract:
Author(s): Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, and Wolfgang Pfaff

Researchers have achieved stable remote entanglement between separate quantum devices. By using a new stabilization technique that mimics a squeezed environment, they can maintain this vital quantum connection even in the presence of real-world imperfections.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031004] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates autonomous stabilization of remote entanglement in a cascaded quantum network using a squeezed-environment-like technique, achieving robust entanglement despite imperfections.
motivation: Remote entanglement is crucial for quantum networks, but maintaining it in the presence of noise and imperfections is challenging. The authors aim to develop a stabilization method that works autonomously and robustly.
method: They implement a cascaded quantum network where two quantum nodes are coupled to a common squeezed reservoir, which effectively provides a continuous and autonomous stabilization mechanism for the entangled state.
result: They achieve stable remote entanglement with high fidelity, even under realistic imperfections, and show that the stabilization is robust against certain types of noise.
conclusion: The work provides a practical approach for maintaining remote entanglement in quantum networks, which is essential for scalable quantum communication and distributed quantum computing.

title: Distributing Stationary Qubit Entanglement Through A Nonlocal Squeezed Reservoir
authors: A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, And J. M. Fink
abstract:
Author(s): A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, and J. M. Fink

A fully autonomous process is demonstrated that entangles two spatially separated superconducting qubits by coupling them to a shared, quantum-correlated microwave reservoir, offering a robust new platform for high-throughput entanglement distribution in future quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031005] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates autonomous entanglement distribution between two superconducting qubits via a shared squeezed microwave reservoir, offering a robust platform for quantum networks.
motivation: Entanglement distribution is crucial for quantum networks, but current methods often require active control or suffer from loss. A fully autonomous approach using a nonlocal squeezed reservoir could provide a simpler and more robust alternative.
method: The authors couple two spatially separated superconducting qubits to a common microwave resonator that is squeezed, creating a quantum-correlated reservoir. They analyze the resulting steady-state entanglement and its dependence on system parameters.
result: They demonstrate that the qubits become entangled in a stationary state, with the entanglement tunable and robust against certain imperfections. The scheme is fully autonomous, requiring no active feedback or measurement.
conclusion: This work establishes a new method for high-throughput entanglement distribution in quantum networks, leveraging hybrid quantum systems and reservoir engineering.

title: Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation In 2d Without Getting Tied In Knots
authors: Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, And Benjamin J. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, and Benjamin J. Brown

Researchers have designed a way to perform complex logic gates in two-dimensional quantum computers by temporarily moving data into an exotic non-Abelian phase. This method provides a path toward large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031001] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a novel scheme for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D using non-Abelian phases, avoiding the need for braiding.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation typically requires complex braiding of anyons in 2D, which is experimentally challenging. The authors aim to simplify this by using non-Abelian phases to perform logic gates without braiding.
method: The method involves temporarily moving quantum information into an exotic non-Abelian phase, where logical operations can be performed via measurements or other means, and then returning to a stable phase.
result: The paper demonstrates a universal set of fault-tolerant gates in 2D without braiding, potentially simplifying the experimental implementation of quantum computers.
conclusion: This approach offers a promising path toward large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computation by reducing the complexity of gate operations in 2D architectures.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity by coupling tin-vacancy centers in diamond to photonic crystal cavities, a key step for scalable quantum networks.
motivation: Efficient spin-photon interfaces are crucial for quantum networks; achieving high cooperativity in nanophotonic devices is a major challenge.
method: The authors fabricate diamond photonic crystal cavities with embedded tin-vacancy centers and characterize the optical and spin properties, measuring the coherent cooperativity.
result: They achieve above-unity coherent cooperativity, indicating strong coupling between the spin and cavity, which is essential for high-fidelity entanglement generation.
conclusion: This work establishes tin-vacancy centers in photonic crystal cavities as a promising platform for scalable quantum networking applications.

title: Constant-Depth Clifford-Hierarchy Gates Via Non-Abelian Surface Codes
abstract:
Author(s): Alison Warman and Sakura Schäfer-Nameki

Using non-Abelian topological order, it is shown that two-dimensional, local, and topologically protected logical gates at any level of the Clifford hierarchy are achievable.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033029] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that constant-depth logical gates at any level of the Clifford hierarchy can be achieved using non-Abelian surface codes, providing a topologically protected approach to universal quantum computation.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires implementing logical gates that are both topologically protected and efficient. Previous schemes for Clifford hierarchy gates often require non-constant depth or lack topological protection.
method: The authors leverage non-Abelian topological order, specifically using non-Abelian surface codes, to design two-dimensional local circuits that implement logical gates at any level of the Clifford hierarchy in constant depth.
result: They show that constant-depth, topologically protected logical gates at any level of the Clifford hierarchy are achievable, which is a significant improvement over existing methods.
conclusion: This work advances the theory of topological quantum computation by providing a systematic method for implementing high-level Clifford gates with constant depth, potentially simplifying fault-tolerant quantum computing architectures.

title: No-Go Theorem On Fault Tolerant Gadgets For Multiple Logical Qubits
abstract:
Author(s): Aranya Chakraborty and Daniel Gottesman

Common classes of fault-tolerant constructions are shown to have fundamental limitations in their ability to implement the full Clifford group.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033027] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves a no-go theorem showing that common fault-tolerant gadget constructions cannot implement the full Clifford group for multiple logical qubits.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires implementing logical gates, but there are known limitations on which gates can be transversally implemented. This work aims to characterize the limitations of a broad class of fault-tolerant gadgets.
method: The authors analyze common fault-tolerant gadget constructions, likely using algebraic and coding-theoretic arguments to show that they cannot generate the full Clifford group.
result: They prove a no-go theorem that restricts the set of logical gates achievable by these gadgets, specifically preventing universal Clifford group implementation.
conclusion: The result implies that alternative approaches are needed for fault-tolerant Clifford group implementation, guiding future design of quantum error correction schemes.

title: Fast, High-Fidelity Transmon Readout With Intrinsic Purcell Protection Via Nonperturbative Cross-Kerr Coupling
authors: Guillaume Beaulieu, Jun-Zhe Chen, Marco Scigliuzzo, Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Alex A. Chapple, Peter A. Spring, Alexandre Blais, And Pasquale Scarlino
abstract:
Author(s): Guillaume Beaulieu, Jun-Zhe Chen, Marco Scigliuzzo, Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Alex A. Chapple, Peter A. Spring, Alexandre Blais, and Pasquale Scarlino

A novel transmon readout architecture leverages nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling to achieve fast, high-fidelity measurement with built-in Purcell protection.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033017] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a novel transmon readout architecture using nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling for fast, high-fidelity measurement with intrinsic Purcell protection.
motivation: Standard transmon readout suffers from a trade-off between measurement speed and Purcell decay, limiting fidelity and scalability. The authors aim to overcome this by exploiting nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling.
method: They design a readout architecture where the transmon is nonperturbatively coupled to a readout resonator via a cross-Kerr interaction, enabling fast measurement while suppressing Purcell decay through a protected mode structure.
result: The architecture achieves fast, high-fidelity readout with built-in Purcell protection, as demonstrated through theoretical analysis and experimental validation.
conclusion: This work provides a promising solution for scalable, high-performance transmon readout, advancing superconducting quantum computing hardware.

title: Chiral Color Code: Single-Shot Error Correction For Exotic Topological Order
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

A family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes achieving single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders is proposed, introducing new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033015] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a family of 3D stabilizer codes that achieve single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders, offering new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: Single-shot error correction is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but existing codes are limited to certain topological orders. The authors aim to extend single-shot error correction to fermionic and chiral topological orders, which are of fundamental interest.
method: The authors construct a family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes, specifically the chiral color code, and analyze their error correction properties, demonstrating that they support single-shot error correction.
result: The proposed codes achieve single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders, which was previously not known to be possible.
conclusion: The chiral color code provides a new platform for fault-tolerant quantum computation, potentially enabling more efficient and robust quantum error correction for exotic topological phases.

title: Accelerating Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation With Good Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, And Ying Li
abstract:
Author(s): Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, and Ying Li

Fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead is enabled by parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033012] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a fault-tolerant quantum computation scheme using good quantum LDPC codes with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead, enabled by parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation typically requires significant overhead in qubits and time. The goal is to reduce these overheads using advanced quantum error correction codes.
method: The authors employ good quantum low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes, which have constant encoding rate and linear distance, and combine them with parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation to achieve efficient fault tolerance.
result: The scheme achieves constant qubit overhead and low time overhead, significantly improving over previous approaches. It demonstrates the feasibility of using LDPC codes for practical fault-tolerant computation.
conclusion: The work advances quantum error correction and fault tolerance, showing that good LDPC codes can enable more efficient quantum computation, which is a core topic in quantum information.

title: Robust Certification Of Non-Projective Measurements: Theory And Experiment
authors: Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, And Nikolai Wyderka
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, and Nikolai Wyderka

A new complete semidefinite programming hierarchy is used to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones, accompanied by an experimental demonstration on a trapped-ion platform.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033005] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a complete SDP hierarchy to certify non-projective measurements and demonstrates it experimentally on a trapped-ion platform.
motivation: Certifying non-projective measurements is crucial for quantum information tasks, but existing methods are limited. The authors aim to provide a robust and complete certification method.
method: They develop a new complete semidefinite programming (SDP) hierarchy that can certify the impossibility of simulating a given measurement by projective ones, and implement it in an experiment with trapped ions.
result: The hierarchy provides a rigorous certification method, and the experimental demonstration validates its practical applicability.
conclusion: The work advances the certification of quantum measurements, with implications for quantum information processing and foundational tests.

title: Quantum Detectors As Autonomous Machines: Assessing The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of Information Acquisition
authors: Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, And Marcus Huber
abstract:
