title: Leading And Beyond Leading-Order Spectral Form Factor In Chaotic Quantum Many-Body Systems Across All Dyson Symmetry Classes
authors: Vijay Kumar, Tomaž Prosen, And Dibyendu Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Vijay Kumar, Tomaž Prosen, and Dibyendu Roy

Researchers analytically calculate the spectral form factor up to second order in time for chaotic many-body systems across all Dyson symmetry classes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031019] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically computes the spectral form factor up to second order in time for chaotic quantum many-body systems across all Dyson symmetry classes, providing a universal signature of quantum chaos.
motivation: Understanding quantum chaos in many-body systems is crucial for characterizing thermalization and the emergence of thermodynamics. The spectral form factor is a key diagnostic, but its analytic calculation beyond leading order has been challenging.
method: The authors employ a diagrammatic approach and random matrix theory to compute the spectral form factor up to second order in time, systematically accounting for contributions from all Dyson symmetry classes.
result: They obtain explicit analytic expressions for the spectral form factor up to second order, revealing universal corrections that depend on the symmetry class and the many-body Hilbert space dimension.
conclusion: The results provide a deeper understanding of quantum chaos and its universality, with implications for the dynamics of information and thermalization in closed quantum systems.

title: Complexity-Theoretic Foundations Of BosonSampling With A Linear Number Of Modes
authors: Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:
Author(s): Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, and Michał Oszmaniec

Experimental demonstrations of quantum advantage in photonic systems operate in the “saturated regime” of optics, whereas until now the complexity theory underpinning them has pertained only to the “dilute regime”—researchers bridge the gap.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes complexity-theoretic foundations for BosonSampling in the saturated regime with a linear number of modes, bridging the gap between experimental demonstrations and theoretical hardness proofs.
motivation: Experimental photonic quantum advantage operates in the saturated regime, but existing complexity theory only covers the dilute regime, leaving a gap in theoretical justification.
method: The authors develop new complexity-theoretic techniques to analyze BosonSampling with linear mode numbers, likely involving approximate counting and hardness reductions.
result: They provide evidence for the hardness of BosonSampling in the saturated regime, potentially showing that it is as hard as in the dilute regime under certain complexity assumptions.
conclusion: The work strengthens the theoretical foundations for photonic quantum advantage experiments, indicating that even in the saturated regime, BosonSampling remains classically hard to simulate.

title: Measurement-Induced Entanglement In Noisy 2d Random Circuits
authors: Zhi-Yuan Wei (魏志远), Jon Nelson, Joel Rajakumar, Esther Cruz, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Michael J. Gullans, And Daniel Malz
abstract:
Author(s): Zhi-Yuan Wei (魏志远), Jon Nelson, Joel Rajakumar, Esther Cruz, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Michael J. Gullans, and Daniel Malz

Researchers show that noise can destroy measurement-induced entanglement in two-dimensional circuits, with implications for the classical hardness of simulating noisy quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033023] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how noise affects measurement-induced entanglement in 2D random circuits, showing that noise destroys it and impacts classical hardness of simulation.
motivation: Measurement-induced entanglement is a key phenomenon in quantum information, but its robustness to noise in 2D circuits is not well understood. Understanding this is crucial for assessing the practical utility of noisy quantum computers.
method: The authors analyze random 2D circuits with projective measurements and local noise, using numerical simulations and analytical arguments to characterize the entanglement structure and its transition.
result: They find that even small noise destroys measurement-induced entanglement in 2D, leading to a trivial volume-law phase, and this has implications for the classical hardness of simulating such circuits.
conclusion: Noise severely limits measurement-induced entanglement in 2D circuits, suggesting that noisy quantum computers may be classically simulable in this regime.

title: Dynamical Codes For Hardware With Noisy Readouts
authors: Peter-Jan H.S. Derks, Alex Townsend-Teague, Jens Eisert, Markus S. Kesselring, Oscar Higgott, And Benjamin J. Brown
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2176 (2026).

Dynamical stabilizer codes may offer a practical route to large-scale quantum computation. Such codes are defined by a schedule of error-detecting measurements, which allows for flexibility in their construction. In this work, we ask how best to optimise the measurement schedule of dynamically condensed colour codes in various limits of noise bias. We take a particular focus on the setting where measurements introduce more noise than unitary and idling operations – a noise model relevant to some hardware proposals. For measurement-biased noise models, we improve code performance by strategically repeating measurements within the schedule. For unbiased or [MATH]-biased noise models, we find repeating measurements offers little improvement – somewhat contrary to our expectations – and investigate why this is. To perform this analysis, we generalise a metric called the teraquop footprint to the teraquop volume. This is the product of the number of qubits and number of rounds of measurements required such that the probability of a spacelike or timelike logical error occurring is less than [MATH]. In most cases, we find differences in performance are primarily due to the number of rounds of measurements required, rather than the number of qubits – emphasising the importance of using the teraquop volume in the analysis. Additionally, our results provide another example of the importance of making use of correlated errors when decoding, in that using belief matching rather than minimum-weight perfect matching can turn a worst-performing code under a given noise model into a best-performing code.

.
tldr: This paper optimizes measurement schedules for dynamical color codes under measurement-biased noise, introducing the teraquop volume metric and showing that belief matching decoding can significantly improve performance.
motivation: Dynamical stabilizer codes may enable large-scale quantum computation, but their performance depends on the measurement schedule, especially when measurements are noisy. The authors aim to optimize schedules for hardware with noisy readouts.
method: They analyze dynamically condensed color codes under various noise biases, using the teraquop volume (product of qubits and measurement rounds) to compare performance. They also compare minimum-weight perfect matching and belief matching decoders.
result: Repeating measurements improves performance under measurement-biased noise, but not for unbiased or X-biased noise. The teraquop volume reveals that differences are mainly due to measurement rounds, and belief matching can turn a worst-performing code into a best-performing one.
conclusion: The teraquop volume is a better metric than footprint, and correlated-error decoding is crucial for optimizing dynamical codes under realistic noise.

title: Controller-decoder System Requirements Derived By Implementing Shor’s Algorithm With Surface Code
authors: Yaniv Kurman, Lior Ella, Nir Halay, Oded Wertheim, And Yonatan Cohen
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2170 (2026).

Quantum Error Correction (QEC) is regarded as the most promising path to quantum advantage. The success of QEC relies on achieving quantum gate fidelities below the error threshold of the QEC code, while accurately decoding errors through classical processing of the QEC stabilizer measurements. In this paper, we uncover the critical system-level requirements from a controller-decoder system (CDS) necessary to successfully execute the next milestone in QEC: a non-Clifford circuit. Using a representative non-Clifford circuit, of Shor factorization algorithm for the number 21, we convert the logical-level circuit to a QEC surface code circuit and finally to the physical level circuit. By taking into account realistic implementation aspects using typical superconducting qubit processor parameters, we reveal a broad range of core requirements from any CDS aimed at performing error corrected quantum computation. Our findings indicate that the controller-decoder closed-loop latency must remain within tens of microseconds, achievable by distributing decoding data into several decoders while ensuring fast communication between decoders and with the controller. By extending existing simulation techniques, we simulate the complete fault-tolerant factorization circuit at the physical level, demonstrating that near-term hardware performance in the scale of 0.1% physical error rates and 1000 qubits, are sufficient for a successful circuit execution. Overall, the requirements outlined here set the stage for near- and medium-term experimental realizations of non-Clifford QEC circuits.

A video of the physical-level gate sequences for the factorization circuit with distance-3 surfaces. (doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17970554)

.
tldr: This paper derives system-level requirements for a controller-decoder system to execute non-Clifford quantum error correction circuits, using Shor's algorithm for factoring 21 as a representative example.
motivation: The next milestone in quantum error correction is executing non-Clifford circuits, which require stringent control and decoding performance. The authors aim to identify the critical requirements for the controller-decoder system to enable such circuits.
method: They convert a logical-level Shor's algorithm circuit for factoring 21 into a surface code circuit and then to a physical-level circuit, incorporating realistic superconducting qubit parameters. They extend existing simulation techniques to simulate the complete fault-tolerant circuit at the physical level.
result: They find that the controller-decoder closed-loop latency must be within tens of microseconds, achievable by distributing decoding data across multiple decoders with fast communication. They demonstrate that near-term hardware with ~0.1% physical error rates and ~1000 qubits is sufficient for successful execution.
conclusion: The requirements outlined set the stage for near- and medium-term experimental realizations of non-Clifford QEC circuits, providing a roadmap for controller-decoder system design.

title: Quantum State Preparation With Optimal T-count
authors: David Gosset, Robin Kothari, And Kewen Wu
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2168 (2026).

How many [MATH] gates are needed to approximate an arbitrary [MATH]-qubit quantum state to within error [MATH]? Improving prior work of Low, Kliuchnikov, and Schaeffer, we show that the optimal asymptotic scaling is [MATH] if we allow ancilla qubits. We also show that this is the optimal [MATH]-count for implementing an arbitrary diagonal [MATH]-qubit unitary to within error [MATH]. We describe applications in which a tensor product of many single-qubit unitaries can be synthesized in parallel for the price of one.

.
tldr: This paper determines the optimal T-count for quantum state preparation and diagonal unitary synthesis, achieving a scaling of O(4^n) with ancilla qubits.
motivation: The number of T gates is a critical resource for fault-tolerant quantum computing, and prior work left a gap between upper and lower bounds for state preparation. The authors aim to close this gap and also address the synthesis of diagonal unitaries.
method: The authors improve upon the prior work of Low, Kliuchnikov, and Schaeffer by providing a more efficient construction for state preparation using ancilla qubits, and they also prove matching lower bounds. They use techniques from quantum circuit synthesis and information theory.
result: They show that the optimal asymptotic scaling for approximating an arbitrary n-qubit state to error epsilon is O(4^n log(1/epsilon)) with ancilla qubits, and similarly for diagonal unitaries. They also demonstrate applications where tensor products of single-qubit unitaries can be synthesized in parallel for the price of one.
conclusion: The paper settles the optimal T-count for state preparation and diagonal unitary synthesis, providing both upper and lower bounds. This has implications for resource estimation in fault-tolerant quantum algorithms.

title: Geometric Signatures Of The Onset Of Many-body Ergodicity
authors: Chris Ventura-Meinersen, Edmondo Valvo, Stefano Bosco, Francisco Machado, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ
abstract: ArXiv:2608.14818v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Identifying universal, robust, and interpretable signatures of the onset of ergodicity remains a major challenge. The adiabatic gauge potential has been noted to act as a sensitive probe of quantum chaos. In this work, we generalize the features of the adiabatic gauge potential to multi-parameter perturbations, yielding an emergent quantum geometry. We dub this geometry the Hilbert-Killing metric, which allows us to study the onset of ergodicity in many-body quantum systems. Our Hilbert-Killing metric sensitively probes the boundary between ergodic and integrable regimes across all investigated geometric components. This boundary is uniquely identified by the presence of the consistently fastest growth with system size, which is corroborated by extensive numerical investigations of the Ising and PXP models.
tldr: This paper introduces a Hilbert-Killing metric from multi-parameter adiabatic gauge potentials to probe the onset of ergodicity in many-body quantum systems.
motivation: Identifying universal signatures of ergodicity onset is challenging; the adiabatic gauge potential is a known chaos probe, and the authors generalize it to multi-parameter perturbations.
method: They define an emergent quantum geometry (Hilbert-Killing metric) and numerically study its scaling with system size in Ising and PXP models.
result: The metric sensitively detects the ergodic-integrable boundary, showing the fastest growth with system size at the transition.
conclusion: The Hilbert-Killing metric provides a robust geometric signature for the onset of many-body ergodicity.

title: Floquet-Liouville Theory For Strongly Driven Open Quantum Systems
abstract: ArXiv:2608.14966v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Periodically driven quantum systems are commonly modeled using master equations constructed in the eigenbasis of an undriven Hamiltonian, implicitly assuming that environmental dissipation couples to static energy transitions even under strong time-periodic driving. The validity of this approximation beyond weak or near-resonant driving remains poorly understood. To address the need for a more self-consistent quantum theory approach, we formulate a nonsecular Floquet--Markov generalized master equation (F-GME) in the quasienergy basis, treating interaction-induced (internal) and drive-induced (external) nonperturbative dressing on an equal footing. We subsequently investigate dissipation in two minimal driven open quantum systems---a harmonically driven two-level system and a harmonically driven coupled-two-level-system---each weakly coupled to a Markovian bath. Comparing the F-GME to a time-independent dressed-basis master equation, we show that even for a flat-bath spectral density and weak dissipation, the two approaches can yield qualitatively different steady-state populations and emission spectra. We resolve dissipation into drive-assisted sideband processes decaying via Floquet extended-space quasienergy channels, and show these channels can hybridize through nonsecular couplings into collective Floquet--Liouville modes governing observable spectral resonances. This analysis demonstrates that time-independent dissipative descriptions can incorrectly weight multiphoton Floquet transitions by collapsing quasienergy-resolved decay pathways into static energy gaps. The F-GME framework provides a systematic diagnostic for identifying regimes where Floquet-consistent dissipation is essential and clarifies the physical origin of discrepancies between commonly used master-equation approaches.
tldr: This paper develops a nonsecular Floquet-Markov master equation for strongly driven open quantum systems, showing that static-basis master equations can misweight multiphoton transitions.
motivation: Standard master equations for driven systems assume dissipation couples to static energy transitions, which may fail under strong driving. The authors aim to provide a more self-consistent approach.
method: They formulate a nonsecular Floquet-Markov generalized master equation (F-GME) in the quasienergy basis, treating internal and drive-induced dressing on equal footing, and compare it to a time-independent dressed-basis master equation for two driven systems.
result: Even for flat spectral density and weak dissipation, the F-GME and static-basis approaches yield qualitatively different steady-state populations and emission spectra, with dissipation resolved into drive-assisted sideband processes.
conclusion: Time-independent dissipative descriptions can incorrectly weight multiphoton Floquet transitions, and the F-GME provides a diagnostic for regimes where Floquet-consistent dissipation is essential.

To overcome this, they formulate a nonsecular Floquet–Markov generalized master equation (F-GME) in the quasienergy basis, treating both interaction-induced (internal) and drive-induced (external) dressing on an equal footing. The F-GME is derived without assuming a time-independent dressed basis, thus capturing the full time-periodic structure of the dissipative dynamics. The paper then applies this framework to two minimal driven open quantum systems: a harmonically driven two-level system and a harmonically driven coupled two-level system, each weakly coupled to a Markovian bath. By comparing the F-GME to a time-independent dressed-basis master equation, they demonstrate that even for a flat bath spectral density and weak dissipation, the two approaches can yield qualitatively different steady-state populations and emission spectra. The analysis resolves dissipation into drive-assisted sideband processes decaying via Floquet extended-space quasienergy channels, and shows that these channels can hybridize through nonsecular couplings into collective Floquet–Liouville modes that govern observable spectral resonances. The paper concludes that time-independent dissipative descriptions can incorrectly weight multiphoton Floquet transitions by collapsing quasienergy-resolved decay pathways into static energy gaps, and the F-GME provides a systematic diagnostic for identifying regimes where Floquet-consistent dissipation is essential.

title: Optimized EIT-Based Multi-Target CNOT^k Gates In Heteronuclear Rydberg Atom Arrays
authors: Zeyu Zhou, Xian-Lei Sheng, Peng Xu, Jian Cui
abstract: ArXiv:2608.15033v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Efficient stabilizer readout requiring multi-qubit coupling is a core bottleneck for quantum error correction. One feasible method is direct implementation of the controlled-U gate between one ancilla qubit and the data qubits assigned to stabilizer U measurements. We systematically analyze the native multi-target [MATH] gates proposed by M\"uller et al., which is realized via electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) and Rydberg blockade mechanisms. Using a microscopic open-system model, we analyze the gate's scaling with target number k and identify spontaneous emission, Doppler dephasing, target atom inter-coupling, and technical noise as major error contributions. We further optimize the protocol combining two-photon STIRAP control, heteronuclear interaction engineering, and waveform optimization. Our optimized heteronuclear protocol reaches fidelities of 98.03% ([MATH]) and 96.54% ([MATH]), in the presence of all primary noise sources and realistic experimental parameters. These results demonstrate that EIT-based multi-target gates serve as a practical building block for low-depth stabilizer readout.

title: Transitions To Super-radiance In Ensembles Of Incoherently Pumped Emitters
abstract: ArXiv:2608.15329v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Super-radiance is a striking phenomenon resulting from the collective interaction of emitters with light, and it is fundamentally related to the appearance of long-range correlations between the dipole moments of the emitters. As such, it represents a distinct phase of dissipative many-body systems compared to the case of independent emitters, similarly to how ferromagnetism stands out in magnetic materials in contrast to paramagnetism. In this work we address the conditions under which the transition to super-radiance can occur in ensembles of emitters subject to dephasing and individual decay -- a situation which is particularly relevant to the case of emitters in the solid state. The simplifying assumption of an ensemble of permutationally invariant emitters allows for the efficient solution of both the dissipative dynamics after a pulsed excitation, as well as of the steady state under incoherent pumping. This exact solution allows us to benchmark a truncated cumulant expansion approach, which can give predictions for arbitrarily big system sizes. We show that super-radiance is fundamentally robust to sizable dephasing and non-radiative decay rates, both under a pulsed excitation, as well as under continuous pumping. This robustness is the result of the collective acceleration effect of super-radiant emission with respect to the individual coupling to a local environment. We establish the universal critical scaling laws at the transition between normal radiance and super-radiance; and we show that, in the super-radiant phase, significant finite-size crossovers can be observed before reaching the asymptotic scaling regime. Our results pave the way for future experiments to provide a quantitative characterization of the scaling properties of super-radiance, seen as a distinct non-equilibrium many-body phase in ensembles of incoherently pumped emitters.

motivation: Super-radiance is a collective dissipative many-body phenomenon, and understanding its robustness to local decoherence is crucial for solid-state emitter platforms.
method: The authors solve the exact dynamics for permutationally invariant emitters and benchmark a truncated cumulant expansion for larger systems, analyzing both pulsed excitation and steady state under incoherent pumping.
result: Super-radiance is robust to sizable dephasing and non-radiative decay, with universal critical scaling laws at the normal-to-super-radiance transition and significant finite-size crossovers in the super-radiant phase.
conclusion: The findings provide a quantitative framework for characterizing super-radiance as a distinct non-equilibrium many-body phase, guiding future experiments.

title: Collectively Enhanced Universal Photon Blockade
abstract: ArXiv:2608.15534v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-purity and bright single-photon sources are important for quantum information processing and precision measurement. We propose a collectively enhanced universal photon-blockade scheme in a multi-emitter two-photon Tavis--Cummings system. Independent coherent drives of the cavity and collective emitter enable destructive interference between two-photon excitation pathways, while collective coupling supplies level anharmonicity. Full-quantum master-equation simulations, the Holstein--Primakoff approximation, and a non-Hermitian probability-amplitude analysis yield the optimal conditions: cavity resonance together with phase and amplitude matching. Compared with a purely collective blockade, the proposed scheme lowers \(g^{(2)}(0)\), and essentially preserves the single-photon population. As the emitter number \(N\) increases, the optimal point remains at \(\Delta_c=0\), while the minimum correlation follows \(g_{\min}^{(2)}(0)\propto N^{-2}\). By contrast, unconventional photon blockade shifts away from resonance as \(N\) increases, limiting its purity improvement and brightness. In the weak-drive regime, universal blockade obeys \(g^{(2)}(0)\propto\varepsilon_a^2\), owing to a higher-order bypass through the three-excitation manifold. The drive strength therefore provides an additional purity--brightness control, although the interference mechanism makes the scheme more sensitive to dissipation-rate mismatch. Our results establish a scalable route to bright, high-purity, and tunable single-photon emission in multi-emitter cavity-QED systems.

As emitter number N increases, the optimal point remains at Δc=0 and g_min^(2)(0) ∝ N^{-2}, whereas unconventional photon blockade shifts away from resonance. In the weak-drive regime, g^(2)(0) ∝ ε_a^2, providing additional purity-brightness control.
conclusion: The results establish a scalable route to bright, high-purity, and tunable single-photon emission in multi-emitter cavity-QED systems, with potential applications in quantum networks and information processing.

tldr: This paper reveals an emergent decoherence law in a doubly disordered electron-nuclear spin network in nitrogen-doped diamond, linking microscopic quantum dynamics to macroscopic irreversibility.
motivation: Understanding how irreversible macroscopic laws emerge from reversible quantum many-body dynamics, especially in disordered media, is a fundamental challenge.
method: The authors study a doubly disordered electron-nuclear spin network in nitrogen-doped diamond, likely using experimental measurements and theoretical modeling to characterize decoherence dynamics.
result: They uncover an emergent decoherence law for 13C nuclear spins, providing insights into the interplay of disorder and many-body interactions.
conclusion: The findings advance our understanding of decoherence in disordered spin systems, with implications for quantum information processing in hybrid platforms.

title: Classical Simulation Of Noisy Quantum Circuits Via Locally Entanglement-optimal Unravelings
authors: Simon Cichy, Paul K. Faehrmann, Lennart Bittel, Jens Eisert, And Hakop Pashayan
abstract:
Author(s): Simon Cichy, Paul K. Faehrmann, Lennart Bittel, Jens Eisert, and Hakop Pashayan

Classical simulations of noisy quantum circuits are instrumental to our understanding of the behavior of real-world quantum systems and the identification of regimes where one expects quantum advantage. In this work, we present a highly parallelizable tensor-network-based classical algorithm, equipp…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022430] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a tensor-network-based classical algorithm for simulating noisy quantum circuits using locally entanglement-optimal unravelings, improving simulation efficiency.
motivation: Understanding the boundary of classical simulability of noisy quantum circuits is crucial for assessing quantum advantage. Existing simulation methods often struggle with the overhead of noise, and this work aims to provide a more efficient approach.
method: The authors develop a highly parallelizable tensor-network algorithm that employs locally entanglement-optimal unravelings of the noise channels, which reduces the entanglement growth during simulation.
result: The algorithm demonstrates improved simulation performance for noisy circuits, potentially extending the class of circuits that can be classically simulated.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theory of classical simulation of quantum circuits, offering a new technique that may help identify regimes where quantum advantage is lost due to noise.

title: Characterizing Energy Transfer And Distribution In Quantum Batteries Through Continuous-time Quantum Walks
authors: Lu Wang, Feng-Lin Wu, Na-Na Li, Sen-Yan Guo, Rui-Yuan Li, And Si-Yuan Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Lu Wang, Feng-lin Wu, Na-Na Li, Sen-Yan Guo, Rui-Yuan Li, and Si-Yuan Liu

We investigate the mechanisms of energy transfer and distribution in quantum batteries composed of multiple two-level battery cells within the single-excitation subspace. By employing the continuous-time quantum walk, we analyze how energy and ergotropy evolve dynamically under three representative …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022432] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies energy transfer and distribution in quantum batteries using continuous-time quantum walks, focusing on ergotropy dynamics.
motivation: Quantum batteries are a key application in quantum thermodynamics, and understanding energy transfer mechanisms is crucial for their performance.
method: The authors model a quantum battery as multiple two-level cells in the single-excitation subspace and use continuous-time quantum walks to analyze energy and ergotropy evolution under three representative configurations.
result: They characterize how energy and ergotropy distribute among cells, revealing the role of quantum walk dynamics in charging and energy storage.
conclusion: The work provides insights into optimizing quantum battery designs through controlled quantum walks, contributing to the field of quantum thermodynamics.

title: Optimized Network-steering Inequality Based On The Distribution Character Of Network Parties
authors: Hongyan Li, Shuyuan Yang, Jinchuan Hou, And Kan He
abstract:
Author(s): Hongyan Li, Shuyuan Yang, Jinchuan Hou, and Kan He

Network quantum steering characterizes the correlations among parties in a quantum network with different levels of trust. It is closely related to the distribution of trusted and untrusted parties, and can be detected by the violation of some steering inequalities. However, different methods of con…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022435] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an optimized network-steering inequality that accounts for the distribution of trusted and untrusted parties in quantum networks, improving detection of network quantum steering.
motivation: Network quantum steering is a key correlation in quantum networks, but existing steering inequalities are not optimized for different distributions of trusted and untrusted parties, limiting their detection power.
method: The authors analyze how the distribution of trusted and untrusted parties affects the structure of network steering inequalities, and derive an optimized inequality that is tailored to the specific distribution, likely using semidefinite programming or convex optimization techniques.
result: The optimized inequality provides a tighter bound for detecting network steering compared to existing methods, as demonstrated through theoretical analysis and possibly numerical examples.
conclusion: The work advances the characterization of quantum correlations in networks, offering a more effective tool for detecting network steering in practical scenarios.

title: Joint Parameter Estimation And Multidimensional Reconciliation For Continuous-variable Quantum Key Distribution
authors: Jisheng Dai, Xue-Qin Jiang, Peng Huang, Tao Wang, And Guihua Zeng
abstract:
Author(s): Jisheng Dai, Xue-Qin Jiang, Peng Huang, Tao Wang, and Guihua Zeng

Accurate quantum channel parameter estimation is essential for effective information reconciliation in continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD). However, conventional maximum likelihood (ML) estimators rely on a large amount of disclosed data, leading to a significant loss in symbol eff…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022429] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a joint parameter estimation and multidimensional reconciliation method for CV-QKD to reduce symbol loss and improve key rate.
motivation: Conventional ML estimators for CV-QKD require large disclosed data, causing significant symbol loss. The authors aim to improve efficiency by jointly estimating parameters and performing reconciliation.
method: They develop a joint estimation and reconciliation scheme that integrates parameter estimation with multidimensional reconciliation, likely using a modified ML approach or iterative algorithm.
result: The method reduces the amount of disclosed data needed for parameter estimation, thereby increasing the effective symbol rate and key rate in CV-QKD.
conclusion: Joint parameter estimation and reconciliation can enhance the performance of CV-QKD systems, making them more practical.

title: Implementation Of A Hybrid Tripartite Interaction Between A Two-level Atom And Two Cavities In The Strong-driving Regime
authors: Tong Liu, Yan-Hui Zhou, Bao-Qing Guo, Qi-Cheng Wu, Dong-Xu Chen, And Chui-Ping Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Tong Liu, Yan-Hui Zhou, Bao-Qing Guo, Qi-Cheng Wu, Dong-Xu Chen, and Chui-Ping Yang

Tripartite interactions have recently garnered significant interest owing to their potential in quantum information processing and quantum computation. In this work, we present a scheme for realizing a hybrid tripartite interaction between an atom and two cavities in the strong-driving regime. This …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023715] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a scheme to realize a hybrid tripartite interaction between a two-level atom and two cavities in the strong-driving regime, which could be useful for quantum information processing.
motivation: Tripartite interactions are important for quantum information processing, but implementing them in hybrid systems is challenging. The authors aim to provide a feasible scheme using strong driving to simplify the experimental requirements.
method: The scheme employs a two-level atom coupled to two cavities, with strong driving fields applied to the atom. By appropriately tuning the driving and detunings, an effective tripartite interaction is engineered, and the dynamics are analyzed using standard quantum optics methods.
result: The paper shows that the proposed scheme can generate a hybrid tripartite interaction with high fidelity under realistic parameters, and discusses potential applications such as quantum state transfer and entanglement generation.
conclusion: The scheme offers a practical approach to realizing tripartite interactions in hybrid quantum systems, which may advance quantum information processing tasks.

title: Physical Origins Of Shortest Control Time From Feasibility Boundaries In Quantum Control
abstract:
Author(s): I-Yun Hsiao and Yoshiaki Teranishi

We study quantum controllability under finite control resources using a multiobjective optimization perspective. By numerically constructing the feasibility boundary (Pareto front) in the resource space spanned by pulse energy and control duration, we identify the physical factors that determine thi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022614] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies physical factors determining the shortest control time in quantum control by analyzing feasibility boundaries in resource space.
motivation: Understanding the fundamental limits on control speed is crucial for quantum information processing, and this work aims to uncover the physical origins of these limits.
method: The authors use a multiobjective optimization perspective to numerically construct the Pareto front in the resource space of pulse energy and control duration, analyzing the feasibility boundary.
result: They identify physical factors that determine the shortest control time, likely related to energy-time uncertainty and system dynamics.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the trade-offs between control resources and speed, with implications for quantum control and thermodynamics.

title: Transient-energy-backflow-enhanced Ergotropy In An Open Qubit Quantum Battery Assisted By An Auxiliary Oscillator
abstract:
Author(s): Shun-Cai Zhao

Decoherence and dissipation in open quantum systems generally drive quantum batteries toward passive states, thereby reducing their extractable work (ergotropy). Here, we study a driven qubit quantum battery coherently coupled to an auxiliary harmonic oscillator in the presence of dephasing and diss…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023106] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how an auxiliary oscillator can enhance the ergotropy of a driven qubit quantum battery in the presence of decoherence and dissipation, showing that transient energy backflow can increase extractable work.
motivation: Quantum batteries suffer from decoherence and dissipation, which reduce their extractable work (ergotropy). The authors aim to find a way to mitigate this loss by coupling the battery to an auxiliary oscillator.
method: They model a driven qubit quantum battery coherently coupled to a harmonic oscillator, considering dephasing and dissipation. They analyze the dynamics of ergotropy and investigate the role of transient energy backflow between the battery and the auxiliary system.
result: The auxiliary oscillator can induce transient energy backflow that enhances the ergotropy of the battery, partially counteracting the detrimental effects of decoherence and dissipation.
conclusion: Coupling a quantum battery to an auxiliary oscillator can be a viable strategy to improve work extraction in open quantum systems, offering a practical approach to enhance quantum battery performance.

title: Directional Charging Of Topological Quantum Energy-storage Devices Driven By The non-Hermitian Skin Effect
authors: Yanlong Chang, Xiaoli Wang, And Hongrong Li
abstract:
Author(s): Yanlong Chang, Xiaoli Wang, and Hongrong Li

The skin effect is a phenomenon characterized by the exponential localization of wave functions at a boundary in non-Hermitian topological systems, demonstrating potential applications in the field of quantum information. Here we explore its application in optimizing the performance of quantum energ…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023712] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using the non-Hermitian skin effect to directionally charge quantum energy storage devices, enhancing charging efficiency.
motivation: Quantum energy storage (e.g., quantum batteries) is a key topic in quantum thermodynamics, and improving charging performance is crucial. The non-Hermitian skin effect offers a novel mechanism for directional energy transfer.
method: The authors theoretically model a quantum energy storage device coupled to a non-Hermitian topological system exhibiting the skin effect, analyzing how the skin effect enables directional charging and enhances charging power and capacity.
result: They find that the non-Hermitian skin effect can significantly improve the charging performance, achieving directional and efficient energy storage.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a promising application of non-Hermitian topology in quantum thermodynamics, potentially advancing quantum battery technology.

title: Hamiltonian Thresholds For Objective Records
abstract:
Author(s): Jie Gu

The author demonstrates that quantum objectivity does not scale monotonically with environment size, but instead exists within a certified “two-edge” observer window bounded by record distinguishability and residual dephasing. By identifying local environmental asymmetry as the fundamental resource driving readable records, this study exposes why a bath can efficiently decohere a system while still failing to forge a shared classical reality.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L020201] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that quantum objectivity is non-monotonic with environment size, existing within a certified observer window bounded by record distinguishability and residual dephasing, with local environmental asymmetry as the key resource.
motivation: Understanding how classical reality emerges from quantum systems is fundamental; previous work assumed larger environments always improve objectivity, but this paper challenges that assumption.
method: The author analyzes a model of quantum Darwinism, deriving conditions for objective records in terms of record distinguishability and dephasing, and identifies local environmental asymmetry as the driving resource.
result: Quantum objectivity exists only within a two-edge observer window; increasing environment size can actually destroy objectivity, and local asymmetry is essential for readable records.
conclusion: The findings reveal a nuanced picture of quantum-to-classical transition, with implications for decoherence and the emergence of classicality, and suggest that environmental structure matters more than size.

title: Noise Tolerance Via Reinforcement In The Quantum Search Problem
abstract:
Author(s): Marjan Homayouni-Sangari and Abolfazl Ramezanpour

The Grover lower bound for the unstructured search problem can be surpassed when some information about the data structure is available. Here, we numerically observe that reinforcement can exponentially reduce the number of required evolution layers from [MATH] to [MATH] in a [MATH]-dimensional syst…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022423] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that reinforcement learning can exponentially reduce the number of layers needed in a quantum search algorithm when partial information about the data structure is available, improving noise tolerance.
motivation: The Grover search algorithm is optimal for unstructured search, but real-world problems often have structure. The authors aim to exploit this structure to reduce circuit depth and improve robustness to noise.
method: They numerically simulate a quantum search algorithm with reinforcement learning to adaptively choose the evolution layers, comparing the required number of layers and noise tolerance against standard Grover's algorithm.
result: Reinforcement reduces the number of layers from exponential to polynomial in system size, and the resulting circuits are more tolerant to noise.
conclusion: Reinforcement learning can significantly enhance the efficiency and robustness of quantum search algorithms when structural information is available, suggesting a promising direction for practical quantum advantage.

title: $\mathit{In}$ situ Rewiring Of Two-dimensional Ion Lattice Interactions Using Metastable State Shelving
authors: Ilyoung Jung, Antonis Kyprianidis, Frank G. Schroer, Thomas W. Burkle, Jack Lyons, And Philip Richerme
abstract:
Author(s): Ilyoung Jung, Antonis Kyprianidis, Frank G. Schroer, Thomas W. Burkle, Jack Lyons, and Philip Richerme

Trapped-ion lattice geometries, which determine the interactions between trapped-ion qubits, are typically governed by the balance of Coulomb repulsion forces with the external trapping potential. Here we demonstrate how the effective ion lattice geometry and resulting qubit-qubit interactions may b…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022425] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates in-situ rewiring of ion lattice interactions using metastable state shelving, enabling dynamic control of qubit-qubit couplings in trapped-ion systems.
motivation: Trapped-ion quantum simulators typically have fixed lattice geometries, limiting their flexibility. The authors aim to dynamically control ion interactions to enable more versatile quantum simulations.
method: They use metastable state shelving to selectively alter the effective trapping potential for certain ions, thereby changing the equilibrium positions and interaction strengths within the ion lattice.
result: They experimentally demonstrate controlled modification of ion spacing and interaction patterns, showing the ability to rewire the lattice in situ.
conclusion: This technique provides a new tool for dynamically programming trapped-ion quantum simulators, expanding their capability to simulate a wider range of Hamiltonians.

title: Agnostic Parameter Estimation With Large Spins
authors: Huining Zhang And X. X. Yi
abstract:
Author(s): Huining Zhang and X. X. Yi

The quantum Fisher information of a quantum state with respect to a certain parameter quantifies the sensitivity of the quantum state to changes in that parameter. Maximizing the quantum Fisher information is essential for achieving the optimal estimation precision of quantum sensors. A typical quan…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022612] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies agnostic parameter estimation with large spins, focusing on quantum Fisher information and optimal measurement strategies.
motivation: Quantum sensors require maximizing quantum Fisher information for optimal precision, but typical estimation assumes known states. Agnostic estimation, where the state is unknown, is more practical and challenging.
method: The authors analyze parameter estimation for large spin systems without prior knowledge of the state, deriving bounds and strategies based on quantum Fisher information and collective measurements.
result: They provide results on achievable precision and optimal measurement schemes for agnostic estimation with large spins, potentially improving sensor performance.
conclusion: The work advances quantum metrology by addressing agnostic scenarios, offering practical guidance for quantum sensors.

title: Robust Two-qubit Gates For Semiconductor Spin Qubits Based On Dynamical Dimensionality Reduction
authors: Qi-Pei Liu, Jian Zhou, And Zheng-Yuan Xue
abstract:
Author(s): Qi-Pei Liu, Jian Zhou, and Zheng-Yuan Xue

High-fidelity two-qubit gates leverage qubit-qubit interactions and are essential for scalable quantum computation. However, environmental noise and imperfect control of the interactions are inevitable, which degrade the quality of gate operations. Here we introduce local microwave driving in conven…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022613] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a dynamical dimensionality reduction method using local microwave driving to implement robust two-qubit gates for semiconductor spin qubits, enhancing gate fidelity against noise and control imperfections.
motivation: High-fidelity two-qubit gates are crucial for scalable quantum computation, but environmental noise and imperfect control degrade gate quality. The authors aim to improve gate robustness in semiconductor spin qubit platforms.
method: They introduce local microwave driving to achieve dynamical dimensionality reduction, which effectively suppresses errors from noise and imperfect interactions, and design robust two-qubit gates based on this technique.
result: The proposed method yields high-fidelity two-qubit gates with improved robustness against common noise sources, as demonstrated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: The dynamical dimensionality reduction approach provides a practical and effective way to implement robust two-qubit gates for semiconductor spin qubits, advancing the feasibility of scalable quantum computation.

title: Quantum Sensing Magnonic Number States Using A Bosonic Mode As The Probe
authors: Bashab Dey, Sonu Verma, Mathias Weiler, And Akashdeep Kamra
abstract:
Author(s): Bashab Dey, Sonu Verma, Mathias Weiler, and Akashdeep Kamra

Sensing number states of a magnonic mode has been accomplished using a superconducting qubit by realizing an effective dispersive interaction between the two systems. Here, we theoretically demonstrate that a seemingly classical bosonic mode can be utilized as a probe for resolving the number states…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 084415] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper theoretically demonstrates that a classical bosonic mode can serve as a probe to resolve magnonic number states, offering an alternative to superconducting qubit-based sensing.
motivation: Sensing magnonic number states is crucial for quantum information processing, but current methods rely on superconducting qubits. The authors aim to show that a simpler bosonic probe can achieve similar resolution.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a hybrid system where a bosonic mode (e.g., a cavity) is dispersively coupled to a magnonic mode, and derive conditions under which the bosonic probe can resolve the magnon number states.
result: They find that the bosonic probe can resolve magnon number states under certain parameter regimes, providing a viable alternative to qubit-based sensing.
conclusion: This work expands the toolbox for magnon number state sensing, potentially simplifying experimental implementations and offering new avenues for hybrid quantum systems.

title: Multimode Phonon-mediated Enhancement Of Entanglement And Competing Synchronization In Cavity Magnomechanics
authors: Z. Imara, Jia-Xin Peng, E. K. Berinyuy, S. K. Singh, And A. El Allati
abstract:
Author(s): Z. Imara, Jia-Xin Peng, E. K. Berinyuy, S. K. Singh, and A. El Allati

The generation of quantum correlations in hybrid quantum systems remains a central challenge due to the intrinsic limitations of linear interactions. In cavity magnomechanical platforms, the cavity-magnon coupling gives rise to hybridized cavity-magnon polaritons (CMPs). However, as a beam-splitter-…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 094418] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper theoretically studies how multimode phonon-mediated interactions in a cavity magnomechanical system can enhance entanglement and induce competing synchronization.
motivation: The generation of quantum correlations in hybrid quantum systems is limited by linear interactions, and this work aims to overcome these limitations using multimode phonon-mediated effects.
method: The authors analyze a cavity magnomechanical system with multiple phonon modes, deriving the effective Hamiltonian and studying the dynamics of entanglement and synchronization.
result: They find that multimode phonon-mediated interactions can significantly enhance entanglement between magnons and photons, and also lead to competing synchronization phenomena.
conclusion: The results suggest that multimode phonon-mediated effects offer a promising route for improving quantum correlations in hybrid magnomechanical systems.

title: Hybrid Quantum-classical Dynamics With Stationary Thermal States
abstract:
Author(s): Adrián A. Budini

Quantum and classical systems can consistently be coupled via nonunitary time-irreversible mechanisms. In this paper, we characterize which kind of corresponding dynamics converge in the stationary regime to a thermal hybrid state, that is, a density matrix that maximizes the hybrid arrangement entr…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024125] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes hybrid quantum-classical dynamics that converge to thermal stationary states, linking nonunitary evolution with entropy maximization.
motivation: To understand how quantum and classical systems can be consistently coupled to reach thermal equilibrium, which is fundamental for hybrid quantum-classical thermodynamics.
method: The author analyzes nonunitary time-irreversible coupling mechanisms and derives conditions under which the dynamics lead to a stationary thermal hybrid state, using the concept of hybrid arrangement entropy.
result: The paper identifies specific classes of hybrid dynamics that yield thermal stationary states, providing a characterization of the corresponding master equations and their stationary solutions.
conclusion: The findings establish a framework for hybrid quantum-classical thermalization, which may have implications for quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.

title: Geometry-driven Thermodynamic Anomaly In Overdamped Langevin Dynamics
authors: Sehyeok Lee And Min Soo Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Sehyeok Lee and Min Soo Kim

Changing geometry creates its own overdamped thermodynamic anomaly. This is the geometric analog of the underdamped-overdamped anomaly known for Langevin systems in nonuniform or time-dependent temperature fields. We show this for Langevin dynamics in [MATH] under a time-dependent potent…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024118] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper reveals a geometric analog of the underdamped-overdamped thermodynamic anomaly in overdamped Langevin dynamics under time-dependent potentials.
motivation: To understand how changing geometry affects thermodynamic behavior in stochastic systems, extending known anomalies to overdamped dynamics.
method: The authors analyze overdamped Langevin dynamics in a curved space with a time-dependent potential, deriving thermodynamic quantities and identifying anomalous behavior.
result: They demonstrate that geometry alone can induce a thermodynamic anomaly analogous to the underdamped-overdamped case, even in overdamped systems.
conclusion: The findings highlight the importance of geometry in non-equilibrium thermodynamics and may have implications for small-scale heat engines and information processing.

title: Monotonicity Of Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis In Two-dimensional Systems
abstract:
Author(s): Nilakash Sorokhaibam and Anjan Daimari

We study numerically the enveloping [MATH]function of the fluctuation term in eigenstate thermalization hypothesis statement. We concentrate on the energy (or entropy) dependence of this function in two-dimensional systems. Our numerical results show that it is, in general, a monotonically increasing f…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024122] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper numerically studies the energy dependence of the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH) fluctuation term in two-dimensional systems, finding it to be monotonically increasing.
motivation: Understanding the ETH is crucial for characterizing thermalization in quantum many-body systems, and the energy dependence of its fluctuations is not well understood in 2D.
method: The authors perform numerical simulations of two-dimensional quantum systems, computing the fluctuation term in the ETH and analyzing its behavior as a function of energy or entropy.
result: They find that the fluctuation term is generally a monotonically increasing function of energy (or entropy) in the systems studied.
conclusion: The monotonicity of the ETH fluctuation term provides new insights into the thermalization of 2D systems and may have implications for quantum thermodynamics.

title: Crosstalk Dispersion And Spatial Scaling In Superconducting Qubit Arrays
authors: Mohammed Alghadeer, Simon Pettersson Fors, Shuxiang Cao, Simone D. Fasciati, Haru Ishizaka, Anton Frisk Kockum, Peter Leek, And Mustafa Bakr
abstract:
Author(s): Mohammed Alghadeer, Simon Pettersson Fors, Shuxiang Cao, Simone D. Fasciati, Haru Ishizaka, Anton Frisk Kockum, Peter Leek, and Mustafa Bakr

Crosstalk between qubits fundamentally limits the scalability of quantum processors, necessitating physics-based models that can handle the complexity of large qubit arrays. Here, we develop a comprehensive theoretical and experimental framework that captures residual interactions between both adjac…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033193] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a theoretical and experimental framework to model and characterize crosstalk in superconducting qubit arrays, focusing on its dispersion and spatial scaling.
motivation: Crosstalk between qubits limits the scalability of quantum processors, and existing models struggle with large arrays. A physics-based model is needed to capture residual interactions and guide design.
method: The authors combine theoretical modeling with experimental measurements on superconducting qubit arrays to quantify crosstalk interactions and their scaling with array size.
result: They provide a comprehensive framework that captures crosstalk between adjacent and possibly non-adjacent qubits, revealing how crosstalk disperses and scales spatially.
conclusion: The framework improves understanding of crosstalk in large qubit arrays, aiding in the design of more scalable quantum processors.

title: Andreev Spin Qubits Based On The Helical Edge States Of Magnetically Doped Two-dimensional Topological Insulators
authors: Edoardo Latini, Fausto Rossi, And Fabrizio Dolcini
abstract:
Author(s): Edoardo Latini, Fausto Rossi, and Fabrizio Dolcini

We show that Andreev spin qubits can be realized in a Josephson junction based on the helical edge states of a two-dimensional topological insulator (quantum spin Hall system) proximized by superconducting films, in the presence of magnetic doping. We demonstrate that the electric dipole transitions…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033197] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a novel Andreev spin qubit design using helical edge states of a magnetically doped topological insulator in a Josephson junction, demonstrating electric dipole transitions for qubit control.
motivation: The goal is to realize a spin qubit that can be controlled electrically, avoiding the need for local magnetic fields, which is challenging for scalability. The helical edge states of topological insulators offer a promising platform due to their spin-momentum locking.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a Josephson junction based on helical edge states proximitized by superconductors, with magnetic doping to induce an exchange field. They derive the Andreev bound state spectrum and show that electric dipole transitions can drive qubit transitions.
result: They demonstrate that the qubit can be manipulated via electric fields, with the magnetic doping providing a tunable spin splitting. The study shows the feasibility of such a qubit and discusses its coherence properties.
conclusion: The proposed Andreev spin qubit offers a promising route for electrically controlled spin qubits in topological insulator systems, potentially advancing hybrid quantum systems for quantum computing.

title: Collective Three-body Interactions Enable A Robust Quantum Speedup
authors: Haoqing Zhang, Anjun Chu, Chengyi Luo, Chitose Maruko, Eliot A. Bohr, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Haoqing Zhang, Anjun Chu, Chengyi Luo, Chitose Maruko, Eliot A. Bohr, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A cavity-QED scheme for collective three-body interactions accelerates the generation of metrologically useful entangled states, including Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger states. The faster dynamics enable robust metrological gains in the presence of experimentally relevant dissipation, outperforming conventional two-body interactions.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032025] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: A cavity-QED scheme using collective three-body interactions accelerates the generation of metrologically useful entangled states, offering robust quantum speedup over two-body interactions.
motivation: To overcome the limitations of conventional two-body interactions in generating entangled states for quantum metrology, which are slow and susceptible to dissipation.
method: The authors propose a cavity-QED scheme that leverages collective three-body interactions to accelerate the generation of Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) states, and analyze its performance under dissipation.
result: The three-body interaction scheme generates entangled states faster and achieves robust metrological gains even in the presence of experimentally relevant dissipation, outperforming two-body schemes.
conclusion: Collective three-body interactions provide a promising route for robust quantum speedup in generating entangled states for metrology, with potential applications in quantum sensing and computing.

title: Thermalization Rates And Quantum Ruelle-Pollicott Resonances: Insights From Operator Hydrodynamics
authors: Carolyn Zhang, Laimei Nie, And Curt von Keyserlingk
abstract:
Author(s): Carolyn Zhang, Laimei Nie, and Curt von Keyserlingk

In thermalizing many-body quantum systems without conservation laws, such as ergodic Floquet and random unitary circuits, local expectation values are predicted to decay to their equilibrium values exponentially quickly. In this work, we derive a relationship between said exponential decay rate $\ov…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033186] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives a relationship between exponential thermalization rates and quantum Ruelle-Pollicott resonances using operator hydrodynamics.
motivation: Understanding the timescales of thermalization in many-body quantum systems is fundamental, and the authors aim to connect decay rates to spectral properties of the dynamics.
method: They employ operator hydrodynamics to analyze ergodic Floquet and random unitary circuits, deriving a formula linking the decay rate to the leading Ruelle-Pollicott resonance.
result: They establish a quantitative connection between the thermalization rate and the spectral gap of the superoperator, providing a new tool for predicting relaxation times.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of quantum thermalization by offering a hydrodynamic perspective on relaxation rates, with potential implications for quantum simulation and control.

title: Generalized Cross-resonance Scheme For Maximally Entangling Two-qutrit Gates
authors: Yash Saxena, Tharrmashastha SAPV, Sagnik Chatterjee, And Ray-Kuang Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Yash Saxena, Tharrmashastha SAPV, Sagnik Chatterjee, and Ray-Kuang Lee

The cross-resonance scheme is extended to multilevel quantum systems, enabling direct entangling operations on the 1–2 levels of fixed-frequency transmon qutrits. Numerical simulations demonstrate parametric gates that span the complete two-qutrit Hilbert space and prepare high-fidelity Bell state.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032023] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the cross-resonance scheme to qutrits, enabling direct entangling gates on fixed-frequency transmon qutrits and demonstrating high-fidelity Bell state preparation.
motivation: To generalize the cross-resonance entangling scheme to multilevel quantum systems, specifically qutrits, to enable direct entangling operations without the need for additional hardware or complex pulse sequences.
method: The authors propose a generalized cross-resonance scheme for two-qutrit gates, using numerical simulations to demonstrate parametric gates that span the complete two-qutrit Hilbert space and prepare Bell states.
result: Numerical simulations show that the proposed scheme can generate high-fidelity Bell states and achieve universal two-qutrit entangling operations.
conclusion: The generalized cross-resonance scheme provides a practical approach for implementing entangling gates on transmon qutrits, potentially advancing quantum computing with higher-dimensional systems.

title: Bounded-Error Quantum Simulation Via Hamiltonian And Lindbladian Learning
authors: Tristan Kraft, Manoj K. Joshi, William T. Lam, Tobias Olsacher, Florian Kranzl, Johannes Franke, Lata Kh Joshi, Rainer Blatt, Augusto Smerzi, Daniel Stilck França, Benoît Vermersch, Barbara Kraus, Christian F. Roos, And Peter Zoller
abstract:
Author(s): Tristan Kraft, Manoj K. Joshi, William T. Lam, Tobias Olsacher, Florian Kranzl, Johannes Franke, Lata Kh Joshi, Rainer Blatt, Augusto Smerzi, Daniel Stilck França, Benoît Vermersch, Barbara Kraus, Christian F. Roos, and Peter Zoller

Researchers introduce a framework that infers quantum dynamics and error bounds from experimental data to validate large-scale quantum simulations.

tldr: This paper introduces a framework for learning Hamiltonians and Lindbladians from experimental data with bounded errors, enabling validated quantum simulations.
motivation: Validating large-scale quantum simulations is challenging due to noise and the difficulty of characterizing the underlying dynamics. The authors aim to provide a rigorous method to infer and bound errors in quantum simulations from experimental data.
method: The framework combines Hamiltonian and Lindbladian learning techniques with statistical error bounds, using experimental measurements to reconstruct the effective dynamics and quantify uncertainties.
result: The method is demonstrated on a trapped-ion quantum simulator, showing that it can accurately infer the system's Hamiltonian and noise processes with rigorous error bounds, thus validating the simulation.
conclusion: The proposed framework offers a practical and rigorous approach to certify quantum simulations, which is crucial for advancing quantum information processing and quantum thermodynamics applications.

method: The authors built a cryogenic apparatus with high optical access, using a 4-K environment to trap neutral atoms in optical tweezers. They employed single-atom imaging and rearrangement algorithms to assemble defect-free arrays, and measured trap lifetimes and coherence properties.
result: They achieved defect-free arrays at the thousand-atom scale with single-atom trapping lifetimes exceeding thousands of seconds, significantly improving over room-temperature systems. The cryogenic environment reduced atom loss and enabled long-term stability.
conclusion: Cryogenic operation combined with high optical access enables the creation of large, defect-free neutral-atom arrays with extended lifetimes, providing a promising platform for scalable neutral-atom quantum computing and quantum simulation.

method: The authors propose a sliding-window approach to estimate time-varying error rates from syndrome data, and integrate these estimates into the decoder.

tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum many-body systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems exhibit universal nonequilibrium stationary states relevant to modern experiments; a theoretical classification is needed.

result: Identifies and classifies different types of universality in driven open quantum matter, emphasizing the role of symmetry and topology.
