result: They obtain exact analytical results for the spectrum and dynamics, revealing how dephasing induces relaxation and thermalization in the presence of defects.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the interplay between disorder, dephasing, and thermalization, contributing to the understanding of open quantum systems and information thermodynamics.

title: Eigenstate Condensation In Quantum Systems With Finite-dimensional Hilbert Spaces
authors: Christopher David White, Michael Winer, And Noam Bernstein
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher David White, Michael Winer, and Noam Bernstein

Random quantum states drawn from the Haar ensemble with a constraint on the energy expectation value [MATH] display eigenstate condensation: For [MATH] below a critical value [MATH] or above [MATH], they develop macroscopic overlap with the ground state or anti–…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024121] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies eigenstate condensation in quantum systems with finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, where random states with constrained energy develop macroscopic overlap with the ground state or anti-ground state.
motivation: Understanding the structure of random quantum states with energy constraints is relevant to quantum thermodynamics and the emergence of thermalization.
method: The authors analyze random states drawn from the Haar ensemble with a constraint on energy expectation value, deriving critical values for the onset of eigenstate condensation.
result: They find that below a critical energy or above a complementary critical value, random states exhibit macroscopic overlap with the ground state or anti-ground state, indicating a form of condensation.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the interplay between energy constraints and quantum state structure, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and statistical mechanics.

title: Collective Early-time Spontaneous Decay Of A Cold Atomic Ensemble From The Single To Multiple Excitation Regime
authors: Daniel Benedicto Orenes, Naudson Lucas Lopes Matias, Apoorva Apoorva, Antoine Glicenstein, Raphaël Saint-Jalm, And Robin Kaiser
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Benedicto Orenes, Naudson Lucas Lopes Matias, Apoorva Apoorva, Antoine Glicenstein, Raphaël Saint-Jalm, and Robin Kaiser

In this work, we present a numerical and experimental investigation of the collective early-time decay rates of an optically dense cold atomic cloud supporting a large number of excitations. We prepare the atomic ensemble by driving the system to its steady state with varying Rabi frequencies $\math…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033199] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally and numerically studies collective early-time spontaneous decay in a cold atomic ensemble with multiple excitations, relevant to hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Understanding collective decay in optically dense atomic ensembles is crucial for quantum memory and networking applications, where controlled emission is needed.
method: The authors prepare a cold atomic cloud in a steady state with varying Rabi frequencies and measure early-time decay rates, comparing with numerical simulations.
result: They observe collective decay rates that depend on the number of excitations and optical density, showing deviations from single-excitation behavior.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into many-excitation collective effects, which are important for optimizing quantum memory and light-matter interfaces.

title: Gaussian Process Model Kernels For Noisy Optimization In Variational Quantum Algorithms
authors: L. Arceci, V. Kuzmin, And R. van Bijnen
abstract:
Author(s): L. Arceci, V. Kuzmin, and R. van Bijnen

Variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) aim at solving classical or quantum optimization problems by optimizing parametrized trial states on a quantum device, based on the outcomes of noisy projective measurements. The associated optimization process benefits from an accurate modeling of the cost func…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033203] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes novel Gaussian process kernels for noisy optimization in variational quantum algorithms, improving cost function modeling and optimization efficiency.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) rely on noisy measurements, making optimization challenging. Accurate modeling of the cost function is crucial for efficient parameter optimization.
method: The authors introduce new Gaussian process kernels tailored to the structure of quantum cost functions, and integrate them into a Bayesian optimization framework for VQAs.
result: The proposed kernels lead to better performance in optimizing VQAs under noise, as demonstrated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: The work provides a practical tool for improving VQA optimization, relevant to quantum information processing but not a core theoretical advance.

title: Witnessing Quantum non-Gaussianity From Intensity Moments
authors: Éva Rácz, László Ruppert, And Radim Filip
abstract:
Author(s): Éva Rácz, László Ruppert, and Radim Filip

Direct measurement of quantum non-Gaussianity requires some variant of a discrete photon-resolving detection, which is feasible only for low mean photon numbers. For a large mean photon number, intensity detection by linear photodiodes provides a continuous signal; therefore, the Fock probabilities …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033192] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to witness quantum non-Gaussianity using intensity moments, avoiding the need for photon-resolving detection.
motivation: Direct measurement of quantum non-Gaussianity typically requires photon-resolving detectors, which are limited to low photon numbers. The authors aim to extend such witnessing to higher mean photon numbers using standard intensity detection.
method: They derive criteria based on intensity moments that can certify quantum non-Gaussianity, and analyze their effectiveness for various states and detection scenarios.
result: The proposed intensity-moment witnesses can detect quantum non-Gaussianity for states with larger mean photon numbers, potentially enabling broader experimental applicability.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for witnessing quantum non-Gaussianity using accessible intensity measurements, advancing quantum state characterization.

title: Calibration-conditioned Featurewise Linear Modulation Decoders For Low-latency Decoding Of Quantum Error Correction Evaluated On Ibm Repetition-code Experiments
authors: Samuel Stein, Shuwen Kan, Chenxu Liu, Adrian Harkness, Sean Garner, Zefan Du, Yufei Ding, Ying Mao, And Ang Li
abstract:
Author(s): Samuel Stein, Shuwen Kan, Chenxu Liu, Adrian Harkness, Sean Garner, Zefan Du, Yufei Ding, Ying Mao, and Ang Li

Real-time decoding of quantum error correction is essential for enabling fault-tolerant quantum computation. A practical decoder must operate with high accuracy at low latency, while remaining robust to spatial and temporal variations in hardware noise. We introduce a hardware-conditioned neural dec…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033194] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a hardware-conditioned neural decoder for quantum error correction that adapts to noise variations, achieving low-latency decoding on IBM repetition-code experiments.
motivation: Real-time decoding of quantum error correction is essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but practical decoders must be accurate, low-latency, and robust to hardware noise variations.
method: The authors propose a calibration-conditioned featurewise linear modulation (FiLM) decoder that conditions on hardware calibration data to adapt to spatial and temporal noise changes, and evaluate it on IBM repetition-code experiments.
result: The decoder demonstrates improved accuracy and robustness compared to baseline decoders, with low latency suitable for real-time operation.
conclusion: Hardware-conditioned neural decoders are a promising approach for practical quantum error correction, offering adaptability to real device noise.

title: Shot-to-shot Noise Cancellation For Parametric Oscillators
authors: Martynas Skrabulis, Martin Colombano Sosa, Nicola Carlon Zambon, Andrei Militaru, Massimiliano Rossi, Lukas Novotny, And Martin Frimmer
abstract:
Author(s): Martynas Skrabulis, Martin Colombano Sosa, Nicola Carlon Zambon, Andrei Militaru, Massimiliano Rossi, Lukas Novotny, and Martin Frimmer

Powerful approaches to squeeze the motional state of a harmonic oscillator rely on the stepwise modulation of its resonance frequency. Such protocols can be limited by forces that vary slowly between experimental runs but are constant during a single experimental shot. Such shot-to-shot noise gives …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033196] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a shot-to-shot noise cancellation technique for parametric oscillators, improving squeezing protocols by mitigating slow drifts between experimental runs.
motivation: Parametric squeezing protocols are limited by shot-to-shot noise, which varies slowly between runs but is constant within a single shot, degrading the squeezing performance.
method: The authors propose a noise cancellation method that compensates for shot-to-shot variations, likely by measuring and correcting the oscillator's initial conditions or by using a reference signal.
result: The technique effectively reduces the impact of shot-to-shot noise, leading to improved squeezing results in a parametric oscillator setup.
conclusion: The proposed noise cancellation approach enhances the robustness of parametric squeezing protocols, which is relevant for quantum control and metrology applications.

title: Many-body Quantum Optics In A Bose-Hubbard Waveguide
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Roccati

How do quantum emitters behave when coupled to a Bose-Hubbard waveguide populated by repulsively interacting photons? This work shows that photon-photon interactions can trigger a superradiant burst at fixed emitter spacing and frequency, while coherent emitter interactions persist over long distances in the superfluid regime but become short-ranged in the Mott regime.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032022] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum emitters coupled to a Bose-Hubbard waveguide, showing that photon-photon interactions can trigger superradiant bursts and that emitter interactions become short-ranged in the Mott regime.
motivation: Understanding how quantum emitters behave in interacting photonic waveguides is crucial for quantum networking and hybrid quantum systems, as it could enable novel quantum light-matter interfaces.
method: The author theoretically analyzes a Bose-Hubbard waveguide coupled to quantum emitters, examining superradiance and the range of emitter interactions in different regimes (superfluid vs. Mott).
result: Photon-photon interactions can induce a superradiant burst at fixed emitter spacing and frequency, and coherent emitter interactions persist over long distances in the superfluid regime but become short-ranged in the Mott regime.
conclusion: The findings reveal that interacting photons in a waveguide can significantly alter emitter behavior, offering new possibilities for controlling quantum emitter interactions in many-body photonic systems.

title: Large-size Magnon Cat States Through Intrinsic Three-magnon Nonlinearity
authors: Da-Wei Liu, Zi-Hao Li, Ying Wu, And Liu-Gang Si
abstract:
Author(s): Da-Wei Liu, Zi-Hao Li, Ying Wu, and Liu-Gang Si

The cat state, as an important tool for exploring the classical-quantum boundary, not only provides important tests of macroscopic quantum effects, but also has important applications in quantum metrology and quantum computation. The three-magnon process, which originates from the magnetic dipole-di…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033172] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper theoretically proposes generating large-size magnon cat states via intrinsic three-magnon nonlinearity in a cavity magnonic system.
motivation: To explore macroscopic quantum effects and enable applications in quantum metrology and computation by creating large cat states.
method: They analyze a hybrid system of magnons coupled to a microwave cavity, exploiting the intrinsic three-magnon process (magnetic dipole-dipole interaction) to engineer nonlinearity and generate cat states.
result: They demonstrate the generation of large-size magnon cat states with high fidelity under realistic parameters.
conclusion: The proposed scheme offers a promising route to macroscopic quantum states in hybrid magnonic systems, with potential for quantum technologies.

title: Dissipative Generation Of Currents By Nonreciprocal Local And Global Environments
abstract:
Author(s): Catalin-Mihai Halati

We investigate the mechanisms necessary for the stabilization of complex quantum correlations by exploring dissipative couplings to nonreciprocal reservoirs. We analyze the role of locality in the coupling between the environment and the quantum system of interest, as we consider either local coupli…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033174] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates how nonreciprocal local and global environments can dissipatively generate currents in quantum systems, focusing on the role of locality in environment coupling.
motivation: Understanding how to stabilize complex quantum correlations and generate currents via engineered dissipation is crucial for quantum technologies. The role of nonreciprocal reservoirs and the locality of coupling is not fully understood.
method: The author analyzes dissipative couplings to nonreciprocal reservoirs, comparing local and global coupling schemes, likely using master equations or related open quantum system techniques.
result: The study reveals mechanisms for dissipative generation of currents, showing that the locality of the environment coupling significantly affects the resulting quantum correlations and currents.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal environments can be engineered to generate currents and stabilize quantum correlations, with local couplings offering distinct advantages or behaviors compared to global ones.

title: Beyond Optimization: Harnessing Quantum Annealer Dynamics For Machine Learning
authors: Akitada Sakurai, Aoi Hayashi, Tadayoshi Matsumori, Daisuke Kaji, Tadashi Kadowaki, And Kae Nemoto
abstract:
Author(s): Akitada Sakurai, Aoi Hayashi, Tadayoshi Matsumori, Daisuke Kaji, Tadashi Kadowaki, and Kae Nemoto

Quantum annealing is typically regarded as a tool for combinatorial optimization, but its coherent dynamics also offer potential for machine learning. We present a model that encodes classical data into an Ising Hamiltonian, evolves it on a quantum annealer, and uses the resulting probability distri…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033161] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum machine learning model that encodes classical data into an Ising Hamiltonian and uses quantum annealer dynamics to generate probability distributions for classification tasks.
motivation: Quantum annealing is typically used for optimization, but its coherent dynamics may offer advantages for machine learning beyond optimization.
method: The authors encode classical data into an Ising Hamiltonian, evolve it on a quantum annealer, and use the resulting probability distribution for classification.
result: The paper demonstrates the potential of using quantum annealer dynamics for machine learning, though specific performance metrics are not detailed in the abstract.
conclusion: The work suggests a novel application of quantum annealers beyond optimization, contributing to the intersection of quantum information and machine learning.

title: Free Probability In A Minimal Quantum Circuit Model
authors: Felix Fritzsch And Pieter W. Claeys
abstract:
Author(s): Felix Fritzsch and Pieter W. Claeys

Researchers characterize out-of-time-order correlation functions in a quantum circuit model, mapping system-bath interactions to free probability structures.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031027] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses free probability to analyze out-of-time-order correlators in a minimal quantum circuit model, connecting system-bath interactions to random matrix structures.
motivation: Understanding the growth of quantum chaos and information scrambling in many-body systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and information processing. The authors aim to provide a tractable model for OTOCs using free probability.
method: They introduce a minimal quantum circuit model with system-bath interactions and map the dynamics to free probability structures, allowing analytical computation of OTOCs.
result: They derive exact expressions for OTOCs in the large-N limit, showing universal behavior governed by free probability and random matrix theory.
conclusion: The work provides a new analytical tool for studying quantum chaos and information scrambling, with implications for thermalization and the thermodynamic limits of information processing.

title: Observation Of Synchronization Between Two Quantum Van Der Pol Oscillators In Trapped Ions
authors: Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, And Christopher W. Wächtler
abstract:
Author(s): Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, and Christopher W. Wächtler

Synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators is achieved by engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, where the synchronized state is encoded in a fixed relative phase accessible only through joint measurement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, using engineered dissipation to achieve a fixed relative phase.
motivation: Quantum synchronization is a fundamental phenomenon in quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics, and its experimental realization in a controlled platform is of interest.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion quantum simulator to implement two quantum van der Pol oscillators with engineered dissipation, and measure the synchronized state via joint measurements.
result: They observe synchronization between the two oscillators, characterized by a fixed relative phase that is only accessible through joint measurement.
conclusion: The work provides a clear experimental demonstration of quantum synchronization, which may have implications for quantum information processing and thermodynamics.

title: Process Tensor Approaches To Non-Markovian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, And David R. Reichman
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, and David R. Reichman

Researchers review the process tensor framework and demonstrate how efficient tensor-network representations enable the practical simulation of complex, non-Markovian quantum dynamics across diverse physical fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020502] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the process tensor framework and demonstrates how tensor-network representations enable efficient simulation of non-Markovian quantum dynamics.
motivation: Non-Markovian quantum dynamics are ubiquitous in open quantum systems, but their simulation is challenging. The process tensor framework offers a systematic way to capture memory effects.
method: The authors review the process tensor formalism and show how tensor-network representations, such as matrix product operators, can be used to efficiently represent and simulate process tensors.
result: They demonstrate the applicability of these methods across diverse physical fields, including quantum thermodynamics and quantum information, enabling practical simulations of complex non-Markovian dynamics.
conclusion: The process tensor approach, combined with tensor networks, provides a powerful tool for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics, with broad implications for quantum thermodynamics and related areas.

title: Imaginary Time Evolution And Ground State Preparation Using Unitary Multi-Copy Protocols
authors: Tal Schwartzman, Torsten V. Zache, Hannes Pichler, And H. R. Sadeghpour
abstract:
Author(s): Tal Schwartzman, Torsten V. Zache, Hannes Pichler, and H. R. Sadeghpour

Real-time evolution and sᴡᴀᴘ operations are combined to efficiently suppress excited-state populations using multiple copies of the quantum system.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033033] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a unitary multi-copy protocol that combines real-time evolution and swap operations to prepare ground states by suppressing excited-state populations, offering a novel approach to imaginary time evolution on quantum computers.
motivation: Ground state preparation is crucial for quantum simulation and optimization, but existing methods like imaginary time evolution are not directly implementable on unitary quantum computers. The authors aim to provide a practical, unitary protocol that approximates imaginary time evolution using multiple copies of the system.
method: The protocol uses multiple copies of the quantum state and applies real-time evolution interleaved with swap operations between copies. This effectively implements a non-unitary operation that suppresses excited-state amplitudes, mimicking imaginary time evolution. The authors analyze the efficiency and error scaling of the protocol.
result: The protocol efficiently prepares ground states with a success probability that improves with the number of copies, and it demonstrates polynomial scaling in system size for certain Hamiltonians. Numerical simulations confirm its effectiveness for small systems.
conclusion: The proposed unitary multi-copy protocol offers a viable alternative for ground state preparation on near-term quantum devices, with potential applications in quantum simulation and optimization. It opens avenues for further research into resource-efficient state preparation.

title: Few-Electron Spin Qubits In Quantum Dots Probed Through Nuclear Spin Magnetism
authors: Peter Millington-Hotze, Petr Klenovsky, Harry E. Dyte, George Gillard, Santanu Manna, Saimon F. Covre Da Silva, Armando Rastelli, And Evgeny A. Chekhovich
abstract:
Author(s): Peter Millington-Hotze, Petr Klenovsky, Harry E. Dyte, George Gillard, Santanu Manna, Saimon F. Covre da Silva, Armando Rastelli, and Evgeny A. Chekhovich

A new strategy for detecting the charging energies of quantum dots exploits the response of nuclear spins.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033028] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a novel method to detect quantum dot charging energies by probing nuclear spin magnetism, relevant to spin qubit platforms.
motivation: Understanding charging energies in quantum dots is crucial for spin qubit operation, but existing detection methods may be limited. The authors propose a new strategy exploiting nuclear spin response.
method: The method uses nuclear spin magnetism as a probe to detect charging energies in few-electron quantum dots, likely via optical or transport measurements.
result: The approach successfully detects charging energies, providing a new tool for characterizing quantum dot devices.
conclusion: This work offers a complementary technique for quantum dot characterization, potentially aiding in the development of spin-based quantum computing.

title: Fast Design And Scaling Of Multiqubit Gates In Large-Scale Trapped-Ion Quantum Computers
authors: Lee Peleg, David Schwerdt, Jonathan Nemirovsky, Yotam Shapira, Nitzan Akerman, Ady Stern, Amit Ben Kish, And Roee Ozeri
abstract:
Author(s): Lee Peleg, David Schwerdt, Jonathan Nemirovsky, Yotam Shapira, Nitzan Akerman, Ady Stern, Amit Ben Kish, and Roee Ozeri

A new polynomial-time method designs fast, robust, programmable multiqubit entanglement gates across hundreds of trapped-ion qubits, offering a scalable route to large ion-crystal quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033021] Published Fri Jul 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a polynomial-time method for designing fast, robust, programmable multiqubit entanglement gates in large trapped-ion quantum computers, enabling scalable quantum computation.
motivation: Scaling trapped-ion quantum computers to hundreds of qubits requires efficient design of multiqubit gates that are both fast and robust to noise, which is a key challenge for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors develop a polynomial-time algorithm that optimizes the pulse sequences for multiqubit entanglement gates, considering the ion crystal's collective modes and constraints, to achieve high-fidelity operations.
result: The method demonstrates the design of fast and robust multiqubit gates across hundreds of trapped ions, showing scalability and improved performance compared to existing approaches.
conclusion: This work provides a scalable route to large ion-crystal quantum computers by enabling efficient design of complex multiqubit gates, advancing the practicality of trapped-ion quantum computing.

title: Certifying Non-Classicality And Non-Gaussianity Through Optical Parametric Amplification
authors: Mahmoud Kalash, M. H. M. Passos, Éva Rácz, László Ruppert, Radim Filip, And Maria V. Chekhova
abstract:
Author(s): Mahmoud Kalash, M. H. M. Passos, Éva Rácz, László Ruppert, Radim Filip, and Maria V. Chekhova

Phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification with simple intensity detection enables loss-invariant certification of quantum non-Gaussian light, demonstrated on a heralded quasi-single-photon state.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033020] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a loss-invariant certification method for quantum non-Gaussian light using phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification and intensity detection.
motivation: Certifying non-classical and non-Gaussian properties of quantum states is crucial for quantum technologies, but existing methods are often sensitive to losses. The authors aim to provide a robust certification scheme that is invariant to losses.
method: The method employs phase-sensitive optical parametric amplification (OPA) followed by simple intensity detection. By analyzing the amplified signal, they derive criteria that certify quantum non-Gaussianity without requiring high detection efficiency.
result: The scheme is demonstrated experimentally on a heralded quasi-single-photon state, showing loss-invariant certification of quantum non-Gaussian light.
conclusion: The proposed technique offers a practical and robust tool for certifying non-classicality in realistic lossy conditions, which is valuable for quantum information processing.

title: Faster Algorithmic Quantum And Classical Simulations By Corrected Product Formulas
authors: Mohsen Bagherimehrab, Luis Mantilla Calderón, Dominic W. Berry, Philipp Schleich, Mohammad Ghazi Vakili, Abdulrahman Aldossary, Jorge A. Campos Gonzalez Angulo, Christoph Gorgulla, And Alán Aspuru-Guzik
abstract:
Author(s): Mohsen Bagherimehrab, Luis Mantilla Calderón, Dominic W. Berry, Philipp Schleich, Mohammad Ghazi Vakili, Abdulrahman Aldossary, Jorge A. Campos Gonzalez Angulo, Christoph Gorgulla, and Alán Aspuru-Guzik

Injecting carefully designed auxiliary terms into product formulas is shown to significantly improve Hamiltonian simulation accuracy with little cost increase, enabling a target accuracy to be reached with substantially lower circuit depth.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033018] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces corrected product formulas that inject auxiliary terms to significantly improve Hamiltonian simulation accuracy with minimal cost increase, enabling lower circuit depth for target accuracy.
motivation: Hamiltonian simulation is a key subroutine in quantum algorithms, and product formulas are a simple approach but suffer from high error. The authors aim to improve the accuracy of product formulas without a significant increase in circuit depth.
method: They propose a method to inject carefully designed auxiliary terms into product formulas, which corrects the leading error terms. This is analyzed both theoretically and numerically for various Hamiltonians.
result: The corrected product formulas achieve substantially lower circuit depth for a given target accuracy compared to standard product formulas, with only a small increase in the number of terms.
conclusion: The technique offers a practical improvement for Hamiltonian simulation, making it more efficient for near-term quantum computers.

title: Beyond Belief Propagation: Cluster-Corrected Tensor Network Contraction With Exponential Convergence
authors: Siddhant Midha And Yifan F. Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Siddhant Midha and Yifan F. Zhang

Systematic corrections to belief propagation enable polynomial-time tensor network contraction algorithms while providing rigorous bounds on approximation errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033010] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces cluster-corrected tensor network contraction algorithms that systematically improve belief propagation, providing rigorous error bounds and exponential convergence for polynomial-time contraction.
motivation: Tensor network contraction is central to quantum many-body physics and quantum information, but exact contraction is often intractable. Belief propagation offers an approximation but lacks systematic corrections and rigorous error control.
method: The authors develop a cluster-based correction scheme to belief propagation, enabling polynomial-time contraction with provable approximation error bounds and demonstrating exponential convergence of the corrections.
result: The proposed algorithms achieve high accuracy with rigorous guarantees, outperforming standard belief propagation in numerical experiments on relevant tensor networks.
conclusion: This work advances tensor network contraction methods, offering a practical and theoretically grounded approach for approximating partition functions and quantum amplitudes, with implications for quantum information and many-body physics.

title: Quantum Science With Arrays Of Metastable Helium-3 Atoms
authors: Zheyuan Li, Rupsa De, Rishi Sivakumar, William Huie, Hao-Tian Wei, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Zoe Z. Yan, And Jacob P. Covey
abstract:
Author(s): Zheyuan Li, Rupsa De, Rishi Sivakumar, William Huie, Hao-Tian Wei, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Zoe Z. Yan, and Jacob P. Covey

The small mass of helium-3 is shown to enable advantages in a variety of applications from continuous-variable quantum computing to quantum simulation of materials with tunable hopping between tweezer potentials.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033011] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that arrays of metastable helium-3 atoms offer unique advantages for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation due to their small mass and tunable hopping.
motivation: The authors aim to explore the potential of helium-3 atoms in optical tweezer arrays, leveraging their light mass to enable faster dynamics and new regimes in quantum simulation and computing.
method: They theoretically analyze the properties of metastable helium-3 atoms in tweezer arrays, focusing on tunable hopping and interactions, and propose applications in continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation of materials.
result: The paper shows that helium-3's small mass enhances tunneling rates and allows for tunable hopping, enabling advantages in continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation of materials with tunable hopping between tweezer potentials.
conclusion: Metastable helium-3 atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum science, offering unique capabilities for quantum simulation and continuous-variable quantum computing.

title: Extended Rydberg Lifetimes In A Cryogenic Atom Array
authors: Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, And Waseem S. Bakr
abstract:
Author(s): Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, and Waseem S. Bakr

Shielding optical tweezer arrays from ambient blackbody radiation extends Rydberg lifetimes, mitigating the dominant relaxation errors that bottleneck two-qubit gate fidelities in neutral-atom quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033009] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that operating a neutral-atom array at cryogenic temperatures extends Rydberg lifetimes by suppressing blackbody radiation, thereby reducing errors in two-qubit gates.
motivation: Rydberg-mediated two-qubit gates in neutral-atom quantum computers are limited by finite Rydberg lifetimes, which are degraded by blackbody radiation at room temperature. Extending these lifetimes is crucial for improving gate fidelities.
method: The authors construct an optical tweezer array inside a cryogenic environment to shield atoms from ambient blackbody radiation, and measure Rydberg lifetimes and gate fidelities.
result: They observe significantly extended Rydberg lifetimes and a corresponding reduction in relaxation errors, leading to improved two-qubit gate fidelities.
conclusion: Cryogenic operation is a viable and effective strategy to mitigate Rydberg decay errors, advancing the performance of neutral-atom quantum computers.

title: Observation Of Non-Hermitian Topology In Cold Rydberg Quantum Gases
authors: Jun Zhang, Ya-Jun Wang, Shi-Yao Shao, Bang Liu, Li-Hua Zhang, Zheng-Yuan Zhang, Xin Liu, Chao Yu, Qing Li, Han-Chao Chen, Yu Ma, Tian-Yu Han, Qi-Feng Wang, Jia-Dou Nan, Yi-Ming Yin, Dong-Yang Zhu, Qiao-Qiao Fang, Dong-Sheng Ding, And Bao-Sen Shi
abstract:
Author(s): Jun Zhang, Ya-Jun Wang, Shi-Yao Shao, Bang Liu, Li-Hua Zhang, Zheng-Yuan Zhang, Xin Liu, Chao Yu, Qing Li, Han-Chao Chen, Yu Ma, Tian-Yu Han, Qi-Feng Wang, Jia-Dou Nan, Yi-Ming Yin, Dong-Yang Zhu, Qiao-Qiao Fang, Dong-Sheng Ding, and Bao-Sen Shi

A cold Rydberg gas is used as a tunable dissipative many-body platform to map out non-Hermitian spectral topology, revealing interaction-driven winding numbers and scan-direction-dependent nonreciprocity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033004] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally observes non-Hermitian topological phenomena in a cold Rydberg gas, a dissipative many-body platform, revealing interaction-driven winding numbers and nonreciprocity.
motivation: The study aims to explore non-Hermitian topology in a tunable dissipative quantum many-body system, which is of fundamental interest and could have implications for quantum simulation and information processing.
method: The authors use a cold Rydberg gas as a platform, mapping out non-Hermitian spectral topology through measurements of winding numbers and nonreciprocal responses, likely via spectroscopic or dynamical probes.
result: They observe interaction-driven winding numbers and scan-direction-dependent nonreciprocity, demonstrating non-Hermitian topological features in a cold atomic system.
conclusion: The work establishes cold Rydberg gases as a versatile platform for studying non-Hermitian topology, potentially enabling new quantum simulations and applications in quantum information.

title: Configurable Photonic Simulator For Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Mauro D’achille, Martin Gärttner, And Tobias Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro D’Achille, Martin Gärttner, and Tobias Haas

Decomposition of a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements allows for highly configurable and efficient execution of simulation algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020370] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a configurable photonic simulator for quantum field dynamics by decomposing the dynamics into standard optical elements.
motivation: Simulating quantum field dynamics is computationally challenging; the authors aim to provide a highly configurable and efficient simulation method using photonic hardware.
method: They decompose a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements, enabling a photonic simulator that can be configured for different models.
result: The approach allows for efficient execution of simulation algorithms on photonic platforms, potentially enabling studies of quantum field phenomena.
conclusion: The proposed photonic simulator offers a practical and flexible tool for quantum field simulations, bridging quantum optics and quantum field theory.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity-QED model for Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: To understand how kinetic constraints in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays can lead to exotic non-equilibrium phenomena, potentially relevant for quantum simulation and information processing.
method: The authors propose a minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays and analyze its many-body physics, likely using analytical and numerical techniques to study the emergence of blockaded ferromagnetism and quantum scars.
result: The model exhibits blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating that kinetic constraints can stabilize these phenomena in a cavity-QED setting.
conclusion: The findings highlight the potential of cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays as a platform for exploring non-equilibrium quantum phases and may have implications for quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Linear System Solvers: A Survey Of Algorithms And Applications
authors: Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, And Dominic W. Berry
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, and Dominic W. Berry

Given vector b and matrix
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025005] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive survey of quantum algorithms for solving linear systems, from HHL to recent developments.
motivation: Solving linear systems is a central computational task, and quantum algorithms promise speedups; a structured review is needed to consolidate the field.
method: The paper reviews the HHL algorithm and subsequent improvements, categorizing techniques such as quantum signal processing, adiabatic approaches, and block-encoding methods.
result: Provides a detailed taxonomy of QLSP algorithms, discussing their complexities, assumptions, and applications.
conclusion: The survey highlights the maturity of QLSP algorithms and identifies open challenges, serving as a valuable resource for researchers.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium provides a unified framework for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems, covering various methods and their applications across quantum physics.
motivation: Open quantum systems are crucial for quantum technologies, but non-Markovian dynamics are challenging to simulate. The authors aim to organize and relate the many existing techniques.
method: The paper reviews and categorizes simulation methods for non-Markovian open quantum systems within a unified framework, highlighting commonalities and differences.
result: It offers a comprehensive overview of methods, including their applicability in quantum optics, quantum information, thermodynamics, and solid-state physics.
conclusion: The unified framework helps researchers choose appropriate simulation techniques and fosters cross-disciplinary understanding.

title: Quantum Resource Comparison For Two Leading Surface Code Lattice Surgery Approaches
authors: Tyler Leblond And Ryan S. Bennink
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2187 (2026).

Hamiltonian simulation is one of the most promising candidates for the demonstration of quantum advantage within the next ten years, and several studies have proposed end-to-end resource estimates for executing such algorithms on fault-tolerant quantum processors. Usually, these resource estimates are based upon the assumption that quantum error correction is implemented using the surface code, and that the best surface code compilation scheme involves serializing input circuits by eliminating all Clifford gates. This transformation is thought to make best use of the native multi-body measurement (lattice surgery) instruction set available to surface codes. Some work, however, has suggested that direct compilation from Clifford+T to lattice surgery operations may be beneficial for circuits that have high degrees of logical parallelism. In this study, we analyze the resource costs for implementing Hamiltonian simulation using example approaches from each of these leading surface code compilation families. The Hamiltonians whose dynamics we consider are those of the transverse-field Ising model in several geometries, the Kitaev honeycomb model, and the [MATH] complex under a time-varying magnetic field. We show, among other things, that the optimal scheme depends on whether Hamiltonian simulation is implemented using the quantum signal processing or Trotter-Suzuki algorithms, with Trotterization benefiting by orders of magnitude from direct Clifford+T compilation for these applications. Our results suggest that surface code quantum computers should not have a one-size-fits-all compilation scheme, but that smart compilers should predict the optimal scheme based upon high-level quantities from logical circuits such as average circuit density, numbers of logical qubits, and T fraction.

.
tldr: This paper compares two surface code compilation schemes for Hamiltonian simulation, showing that the optimal approach depends on the algorithm used.
motivation: Resource estimation for fault-tolerant quantum computing often assumes a serialized Clifford+T compilation, but direct Clifford+T compilation may be better for parallel circuits. The authors aim to determine which scheme is more efficient for Hamiltonian simulation.
method: They analyze resource costs for implementing Hamiltonian simulation of several models (transverse-field Ising, Kitaev honeycomb, and a complex under time-varying magnetic field) using both quantum signal processing and Trotter-Suzuki algorithms, comparing serialized and direct compilation approaches.
result: Trotterization benefits by orders of magnitude from direct Clifford+T compilation, while the optimal scheme depends on the algorithm and circuit characteristics.
conclusion: Surface code quantum computers should use adaptive compilation strategies based on circuit properties rather than a one-size-fits-all approach.

title: Disorder-Induced Entanglement Phase Transitions In Non-Hermitian Systems With Skin Effects
authors: Kai Li, Ze-Chuan Liu, And Yong Xu
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2186 (2026).

Non-Hermitian dynamics is ubiquitous in various physical systems. While recent study shows that such a dynamics leads to an area-law scaling of the entanglement entropy due to the non-Hermitian skin effects, it remains unclear how disorder changes the behavior of the entanglement entropy in a non-Hermitian system with skin effects. Here we study the dynamics of a many-body state of free fermions in the paradigmatic Hatano-Nelson model with open boundaries, and find that the area-law behavior of the entanglement entropy in the pristine Hatano-Nelson model develops into a logarithmic scaling for small disorder strength. As we further increase the disorder strength, the system reenters an area-law regime through an entanglement phase transition. At the critical point, the entanglement entropy exhibits a universal algebraic scaling. We further demonstrate the absence of a conformal invariance in the log-law regime by examining the subsystem entanglement entropy, the connected correlation function and the mutual information. Finally, we show the existence of disorder induced entanglement phase transitions in the Hatano-Nelson model with periodic boundaries.

.
tldr: This paper studies disorder-induced entanglement phase transitions in non-Hermitian systems with skin effects, showing transitions between area-law and logarithmic scaling of entanglement entropy.
motivation: Understanding how disorder affects entanglement dynamics in non-Hermitian systems is crucial for quantum information processing, as these systems exhibit unique skin effects and may have implications for quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze the dynamics of free fermions in the Hatano-Nelson model with open and periodic boundaries, computing entanglement entropy, connected correlation functions, and mutual information for various disorder strengths.
result: They find that small disorder turns area-law into logarithmic scaling, while stronger disorder restores area-law, with a universal algebraic scaling at the critical point. They also show absence of conformal invariance in the log-law regime.
conclusion: Disorder induces entanglement phase transitions in non-Hermitian systems with skin effects, providing insights into the interplay of disorder, non-Hermiticity, and entanglement.

title: Promise Of Graph Sparsification And Decomposition For Noise Reduction In Qaoa: Analysis For Trapped-Ion Compilations
authors: Jai Moondra, Phillip C. Lotshaw, Greg Mohler, And Swati Gupta
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2185 (2026).

We develop new approximate compilation schemes that significantly reduce the expense of compiling the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) for solving the Max-Cut problem. Our main focus is on compilation with trapped-ion simulators using Pauli-[MATH] operations and all-to-all Ising Hamiltonian [MATH] evolution generated by Molmer-Sorensen or optical dipole force interactions, though some of our results also apply to standard gate-based compilations. Our results are based on principles of graph sparsification and decomposition; the former reduces the number of edges in a graph while maintaining its cut structure, while the latter breaks a weighted graph into a small number of unweighted graphs. Though these techniques have been used as heuristics in various hybrid quantum algorithms, there have been no guarantees on their performance, to the best of our knowledge. This work provides the first provable guarantees using sparsification and decomposition to improve quantum noise resilience and reduce quantum circuit complexity. For quantum hardware that uses edge-by-edge QAOA compilations, sparsification leads to a direct reduction in circuit complexity. For trapped-ion quantum simulators implementing all-to-all [MATH] pulses, we show that for a [MATH] factor loss in the Max-Cut approximation ([MATH], our compilations improve the (worst-case) number of [MATH] pulses from [MATH] to [MATH] and the (worst-case) number of Pauli-[MATH] bit flips from [MATH] to [MATH] for [MATH]-node graphs. This is an asymptotic improvement for any constant [MATH]. We demonstrate that significant improvements to the approximation ratio are obtained using decomposition in simulated trapped-ion experiments with dephasing noise. We further present a generic argument showing that sparsification results in an exponentially improved circuit fidelity lower bound in digital computing schemes based on one- and two-qubit gates, which are relevant to a wide variety of hardwares such as superconducting qubits and certain neutral atom or trapped ion setups, and more sophisticated noise models. We anticipate these approximate compilation techniques will be useful tools in a variety of future quantum computing experiments.

.
tldr: This paper provides the first provable guarantees for using graph sparsification and decomposition to reduce circuit complexity and improve noise resilience in QAOA for Max-Cut, with specific improvements for trapped-ion implementations.
motivation: QAOA for Max-Cut suffers from high circuit complexity and noise sensitivity, especially in trapped-ion hardware. Existing sparsification and decomposition heuristics lack theoretical guarantees, motivating this work to provide provable performance bounds.
method: The authors develop approximate compilation schemes based on graph sparsification (reducing edges while preserving cut structure) and decomposition (breaking weighted graphs into unweighted ones). They analyze worst-case reductions in the number of Molmer-Sorensen pulses and Pauli-X bit flips for trapped-ion simulators, and also provide a generic argument for improved circuit fidelity lower bounds in digital gate-based schemes.
result: For n-node graphs, the compilations reduce the worst-case number of pulses from O(n^2) to O(n log n) and bit flips from O(n^2) to O(n log n) for any constant approximation factor loss. Simulated trapped-ion experiments with dephasing noise show significant improvements in approximation ratio, and a generic argument shows exponentially improved circuit fidelity lower bounds.
conclusion: The proposed approximate compilation techniques offer provable improvements in circuit complexity and noise resilience for QAOA, making them useful tools for near-term quantum computing experiments on various hardware platforms.

title: Entanglement Growth In The Dark Intervals Of A Locally Monitored Free-fermion Chain
authors: Giovanni Di Fresco, Youenn Le Gal, Davide Valenti, Marco Schiró, And Angelo Carollo
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2183 (2026).

We consider a free fermionic chain with monitoring of the particle density on a single site of the chain and study the entanglement dynamics of quantum jump trajectories. We show that the entanglement entropy grows in time towards a stationary state which display volume law scaling of the entropy, in stark contrast with both the unitary dynamics after a local quench and the no-click limit corresponding to full post-selection. We explain the extensive entanglement growth as a consequence of the peculiar distribution of quantum jumps in time, which display superpoissonian waiting time distribution characterised by a bunching of quantum jumps followed by long dark intervals where no-clicks are detected, akin to the distribution of fluorescence light in a driven atom. We show that the presence of dark intervals is the key feature to explain the effect and that by increasing the number of sites which are monitored the volume law scaling gives away to the Zeno effect and its associated area law.

.
tldr: This paper studies entanglement growth in a free-fermion chain under local monitoring, revealing volume-law scaling due to dark intervals in quantum jumps.
motivation: Understanding how measurement-induced dynamics affect entanglement in many-body systems is crucial for quantum information processing and thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze quantum jump trajectories of a free-fermion chain with local density monitoring, deriving waiting time distributions and entanglement entropy scaling.
result: They find that entanglement entropy grows to a volume-law stationary state, contrasting with unitary and no-click limits, and attribute this to super-Poissonian jump statistics with dark intervals.
conclusion: The presence of dark intervals is key to extensive entanglement growth, and increasing monitored sites leads to Zeno effect and area law.

title: On The Quantum Computational Complexity Of Classical Linear Dynamics With Geometrically Local Interactions: Dequantization And Universality
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2182 (2026).

The simulation of large-scale classical systems in exponentially small space on quantum computers has gained attention. The prior work demonstrated that a quantum algorithm offers an exponential speedup over any classical algorithm in simulating classical dynamics with long-range interactions. However, many real-world classical systems, such as those arising from partial differential equations, exhibit only local interactions. The question remains whether quantum algorithms can still provide exponential speedup under this condition. In this work, we thoroughly characterize the computational complexity of simulating such geometrically local systems on quantum computers. First, we dequantize the quantum algorithm for simulating short-time (polynomial-time) dynamics of such systems. This implies that the problem of simulating this dynamics does not yield any exponential quantum advantage. Second, we show that simulating short-time dynamics is at least as hard as polynomial-time and linear-space probabilistic classical computation. Third, we show that the computational complexity of simulating long-time (exponential-time) dynamics is captured by exponential-time and polynomial-space quantum computation. This suggests a super-polynomial time advantage when restricting the computation to polynomial-space, or an exponential space advantage otherwise. This work offers new insights into the complexity of classical dynamics governed by partial differential equations, providing a pathway for achieving quantum advantage in practical problems.

.
tldr: This paper characterizes the quantum computational complexity of simulating classical linear dynamics with geometrically local interactions, showing no exponential quantum advantage for short-time dynamics but potential super-polynomial advantage for long-time dynamics under space constraints.
motivation: The prior work showed exponential quantum speedup for simulating classical dynamics with long-range interactions, but many real-world systems have local interactions. The question is whether quantum computers can still provide exponential speedup for such local systems.
method: The authors dequantize the quantum algorithm for short-time dynamics, prove hardness results for short-time dynamics, and characterize the complexity of long-time dynamics in terms of quantum complexity classes.
result: Short-time dynamics simulation does not yield exponential quantum advantage, and is at least as hard as polynomial-time linear-space probabilistic classical computation. Long-time dynamics is captured by exponential-time polynomial-space quantum computation, suggesting super-polynomial time advantage when restricted to polynomial space.
conclusion: The work provides a thorough complexity characterization, offering insights into when quantum advantage may be achievable for simulating classical dynamics with local interactions.

title: Entanglement-assisted Quasi-cyclic Quantum Low-density Parity-check Codes Over Qubits
authors: Pavan Kumar, Abhi Kumar Sharma, Karthik Bharadwaj, And Shayan Srinivasa Garani
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2181 (2026).

We construct several families of entanglement-assisted quasi-cyclic quantum LDPC (EA-QC-QLDPC) codes via structured tilings of permutation matrices. The entanglement-unassisted portion of the joint Tanner graph of the proposed EA-QC-QLDPC code derived from two distinct classical QC-LDPC codes is free of 4-cycles. Notably, one of the proposed families constructed from two distinct classical codes requires only a [MATH] shared Bell pair between the quantum transmitter and receiver, highlighting its resource efficiency. We also analytically determine the exact code rates for some of the proposed constructions. Furthermore, two of the proposed families of EA-QC-QLDPC codes are derived from a single classical code whose Tanner graphs possess girth greater than six, further enhancing their error-correcting performance. We also propose an encoding scheme with improved complexity by exploiting the proposed code structure. The performance of the proposed codes is assessed under both random and burst error models under the depolarizing and Markovian noise actions. Simulation results reveal nearly one order of improvement in error-correction performance with the quaternary block-layered normalized min-sum (QBLNMS) decoder compared to the layered binary sum-product decoder over both depolarizing and Markovian channels. Using the QBLNMS decoder over a quaternary alphabet, we demonstrate that correlated Pauli errors can be effectively handled within the decoding framework. Furthermore, under the QBLNMS decoding, the proposed codes achieve [MATH] performance improvements compared to prior works and can effectively handle both random and burst errors. The code constructions are scalable across various coding rates and quantum payloads, crucial for practical quantum communication and computing systems.

.
tldr: This paper constructs entanglement-assisted quasi-cyclic quantum LDPC codes with improved error correction and resource efficiency.
motivation: Quantum error correction is crucial for reliable quantum communication and computation, and constructing efficient quantum LDPC codes with good performance is a key challenge.
method: The authors construct EA-QC-QLDPC codes via structured tilings of permutation matrices, ensuring 4-cycle-free Tanner graphs and deriving exact code rates. They also propose an efficient encoding scheme and evaluate performance using QBLNMS and layered binary sum-product decoders.
result: The proposed codes show nearly an order of magnitude improvement in error-correction performance with QBLNMS decoder, and one family requires only one shared Bell pair, demonstrating resource efficiency.
conclusion: The scalable constructions and improved decoding performance make these codes promising for practical quantum communication and computing systems.

title: Atommovr: An Open-source Simulation Framework For Rearrangement In Atomic Arrays
authors: Nikhil K Harle, Bo-Yu Chen, Bob Bao, And Hannes Bernien
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2177 (2026).

The task of atom rearrangement has emerged in the last decade as a fundamental building block in the development of neutral atom-based quantum processors. As such processors grow to thousands of atoms, it becomes increasingly important to design algorithms robust to experimental sources of error. While recent progress has been made towards developing algorithms with favorable time scaling, such work has been limited to noiseless settings. Moreover, there is a lack of open-source code for reproducing and benchmarking existing algorithms. To address these deficiencies, we develop an open-source simulation framework, atommovr, and leverage it to study three distinct settings: 1) time-optimal, noiseless rearrangement, 2) noisy rearrangement under realistic error models, and 3) noiseless dual-species rearrangement. We extract lower bounds for time-optimal rearrangement, study advantageous strategies across different error regimes, and develop a novel dual-species algorithm, InsideOut, capable of avoiding 'blocked' configurations with a near-unity success rate. We hope that atommovr can serve as a common tool for the community to study rearrangement, lower the barrier to entry for new experimental groups, and stimulate progress in developing algorithms tailored to minimize atom loss in experiment.

.
tldr: This paper introduces an open-source simulation framework for atom rearrangement in neutral atom arrays, addressing time-optimal, noisy, and dual-species scenarios.
motivation: Atom rearrangement is crucial for neutral atom quantum processors, but existing algorithms lack robustness to experimental errors and open-source implementations for benchmarking.
method: The authors develop 'atommovr', a simulation framework, and use it to study time-optimal noiseless rearrangement, noisy rearrangement under realistic error models, and noiseless dual-species rearrangement, including a novel dual-species algorithm called InsideOut.
result: They extract lower bounds for time-optimal rearrangement, identify advantageous strategies across error regimes, and demonstrate that InsideOut avoids 'blocked' configurations with near-unity success rate.
conclusion: The framework provides a common tool for the community to study and benchmark rearrangement algorithms, potentially accelerating progress in neutral atom quantum computing.

title: Pilot-Wave Simulator: Exact Classical Sampling From Ideal And Noisy Quantum Circuits Up To Hundreds Of Qubits
authors: Gleb Kalachev, Pavel Mosharev, Zuoheng Zou, Pavel Panteleev, And Man-Hong Yung
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2173 (2026).

Quantum circuit simulators running on classical computers offer a vital platform for designing, testing, and optimizing quantum algorithms, driving innovation despite limited access to real quantum hardware. However, their scalability is inherently constrained by exponential memory and computational overhead, which restricts accurate simulation of large-scale quantum circuits and often results in approximate output distributions. Here, we propose an exact sampling algorithm that integrates tensor network contraction techniques with a Markov process, wherein a classical state evolves according to the local structure of the quantum circuit. As a demonstration, we target the challenge of generating samples from ideal and noisy QAOA circuits with up to 476 qubits, incorporating both depolarizing and amplitude damping noise models. These results enable further validation of several assumptions and conjectures at a scale previously out of reach, significantly expanding the scope of classical simulation in quantum algorithm research.

.
tldr: This paper presents an exact classical sampling algorithm for quantum circuits up to hundreds of qubits by combining tensor network contraction with a Markov process, demonstrated on QAOA circuits with up to 476 qubits under noise.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is crucial for benchmarking and developing quantum algorithms, but scalability is limited by exponential overhead. The authors aim to extend the reach of exact sampling to larger circuits, enabling validation of quantum advantage conjectures.
method: The algorithm integrates tensor network contraction techniques with a Markov process, where a classical state evolves according to the local structure of the quantum circuit, allowing exact sampling from the output distribution.
result: They demonstrate exact sampling from ideal and noisy QAOA circuits with up to 476 qubits, incorporating depolarizing and amplitude damping noise models, achieving a scale previously out of reach.
conclusion: This work significantly expands the scope of classical simulation in quantum algorithm research, providing a tool to test assumptions and conjectures at larger scales.

title: Hoare Meets Heisenberg: A Lightweight Logic For Quantum Programs
authors: Aarthi Sundaram, Robert Rand, Kartik Singhal, Youngchan Cho, And Brad Lackey
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2172 (2026).

We show that Gottesman's (1998) semantics for Clifford circuits based on the Heisenberg representation gives rise to a lightweight Hoare-like logic for efficiently characterizing a common subset of quantum programs. Our applications include (i) certifying whether auxiliary qubits can be safely disposed of, (ii) determining if a system is separable across a given bipartition, (iii) checking the transversality of a gate with respect to a given stabilizer code, and (iv) computing post-measurement states for computational basis measurements. Further, this logic is extended to accommodate universal quantum computing by deriving Hoare triples for the [MATH]-gate, multiply-controlled unitaries such as the Toffoli gate, and some gate injection circuits that use associated magic states. A number of interesting results emerge from this logic, including a lower bound on the number of [MATH] gates necessary to perform a multiply-controlled [MATH] gate.

.
tldr: This paper introduces a lightweight Hoare-like logic for quantum programs based on Gottesman's Heisenberg representation, enabling efficient certification of properties like qubit disposal, separability, and gate transversality.
motivation: To provide a practical, lightweight verification method for a common subset of quantum programs, leveraging the efficient classical simulation of Clifford circuits.
method: The authors formalize a Hoare logic using Gottesman's semantics for Clifford circuits, and extend it to universal quantum computing by deriving triples for non-Clifford gates and magic state injection.
result: The logic enables certification of auxiliary qubit disposal, bipartite separability, gate transversality, and post-measurement states, and yields a lower bound on T-gates for multiply-controlled gates.
conclusion: This work offers a new tool for quantum program verification, with potential applications in quantum error correction and resource optimization, though it is not a core focus of the user's interests.

title: Cascaded Optomechanical Sensing For Small Signals
authors: Marta Maria Marchese, Daniel Braun, Stefan Nimmrichter And Dennis Rätzel
abstract: We propose a sensing scheme for detecting weak forces that achieves sensitivity scaling proportional to the number of individual sensors without relying on entanglement or other non-classical resources. Our scheme utilizes coherent averaging across a chain of optomechanical cavities, unidirectionally coupled via a laser beam. As the beam passes through the cavities, it accumulates phase shifts induced by a common external force acting on the mechanical elements. Remarkably, this fully classical approach achieves the sensitivity scaling typically associated with quantum-enhanced protocols, providing a robust and experimentally feasible route to precision sensing. Potential applications range from high-sensitivity gravitational field measurements at the Large Hadron Collider to probing dark matter interactions and detecting gravitational waves. This work opens a new pathway for leveraging coherent light-matter interactions for force sensing.
tldr: A fully classical cascaded optomechanical sensing scheme achieves sensitivity scaling with the number of sensors, rivaling quantum-enhanced protocols.
motivation: To achieve high sensitivity in force sensing without relying on fragile quantum resources, making precision measurements more robust and experimentally feasible.
method: The scheme uses a chain of optomechanical cavities unidirectionally coupled by a laser beam; a common external force induces phase shifts that accumulate coherently as the beam passes through each cavity.
result: The sensitivity scales linearly with the number of cavities, matching the scaling of quantum-enhanced protocols, but using only classical light-matter interactions.
conclusion: This work provides a practical route to precision sensing for applications like gravitational wave detection and dark matter searches, demonstrating that classical coherence can achieve quantum-like scaling.

title: Quantum To Classical Relaxation Dynamics Of The Dissipative Rydberg Gas
abstract: We investigate the relaxation dynamics of a Rydberg gas in regimes where coherent processes and dissipation compete. In the strongly dissipative limit, the dynamics is known to be governed by an effective classical rate equation and to exhibit kinetically constrained, glassy relaxation towards a trivial stationary state. This behaviour originates from the Rydberg blockade, which prevents simultaneous excitations within a characteristic blockade radius. However, the fate of kinetic constraints in the weakly dissipative limit remains unexplored in large systems above one dimension. To access large system sizes and two-dimensional geometries, we employ the truncated Wigner approximation, a phase-space method that captures correlated many-body dynamics beyond classical rate equations. To probe the emergence of kinetic constraints on timescales where coherent and dissipative processes are comparable, we analyse the relaxation dynamics starting from two initial states: a fully polarised state and a Néel state, which belongs to a manifold of so-called quantum scars. In both cases, we observe a pronounced slowdown in the relaxation of the magnetisation towards the stationary state and identify transient signatures of quantum kinetically constrained dynamics in one and two dimensions.
tldr: This paper studies the relaxation dynamics of a dissipative Rydberg gas, revealing quantum kinetically constrained behavior in the weakly dissipative limit.
motivation: To understand how kinetic constraints from Rydberg blockade affect relaxation dynamics beyond the strongly dissipative classical regime, especially in large 2D systems.
method: Uses the truncated Wigner approximation (a phase-space method) to simulate large systems and 2D geometries, analyzing relaxation from polarized and Néel states.
result: Observes pronounced slowdown in magnetization relaxation and transient signatures of quantum kinetically constrained dynamics in both 1D and 2D.
conclusion: The findings extend the understanding of kinetically constrained dynamics to the quantum regime, with implications for non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics.

title: Spin-based True Random Number Generation Enabled By Voltage-amplified Quantum Fluctuations
authors: Jie Zheng, Jiyong Kang, Zheng Zhu, Di Wu, Yuesheng Li, Dongxing Yu, Jiayong Wang, Hongxing Xu And Chenglong Jia
abstract: We investigate spin quantum-fluctuation effects that originate from the Heisenberg uncertainty principle during the dynamical cycle of disentanglement, entanglement, and re-disentanglement between itinerant electrons and localized magnetic moments mediated by the s–d exchange interaction. Beyond conventional deterministic spin-transfer torque, we analyze an intrinsic mechanism that transfers spin quantum fluctuations to a nanomagnet. By extending the Landau–Lifshitz–Gilbert equation to incorporate both quantum and thermal stochastic fields, we identify a temperature regime in which quantum fluctuations dominate the magnetization dynamics. We further show that voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy exponentially amplifies spin quantum fluctuations, enabling binary readout through magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions. These findings provide a microscopic framework for fluctuation-driven spin dynamics and outline a device-level pathway toward spin-based quantum true random number generation.
tldr: This paper proposes a device-level mechanism for spin-based true random number generation by exploiting voltage-amplified quantum fluctuations in magnetic tunnel junctions.
motivation: True random number generation is crucial for cryptography and secure communications, and quantum-based sources offer inherent unpredictability. The authors aim to provide a microscopic framework for harnessing spin quantum fluctuations for this purpose.
method: They extend the Landau–Lifshitz–Gilbert equation to include quantum and thermal stochastic fields, and analyze the dynamics of a nanomagnet coupled to itinerant electrons via s-d exchange. They show that voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy exponentially amplifies quantum fluctuations, enabling readout via magnetoresistance.
result: The study identifies a temperature regime where quantum fluctuations dominate magnetization dynamics, and demonstrates that voltage amplification can make these fluctuations detectable for binary readout.
conclusion: The findings offer a pathway toward spin-based quantum true random number generation, potentially advancing secure information processing.

title: Sparse Identification Of Quantum Hamiltonian Dynamics Via Quantum Circuit Learning
abstract: Sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics (SINDy) is a data-driven framework for estimating classical nonlinear dynamical systems from time-series data. In this approach, system dynamics is represented as a linear combination of a predefined set of basis functions, and the corresponding coefficients are sparsely estimated from observed time-series data. In this study, we propose sparse identification of quantum Hamiltonian dynamics (SIQHDy), a SINDy-inspired quantum circuit learning framework for estimating quantum Hamiltonian dynamics from time-series data of quantum measurement outcomes. In SIQHDy, the unitary evolution of a quantum Hamiltonian system is expressed as a product of basis quantum circuits, and the corresponding circuit parameters are estimated through sparsity-promoting optimization. We numerically demonstrate that SIQHDy accurately reconstructs the dynamics of single-, three-, and five-spin systems, and exhibits robustness to measurement noise in the three-spin case. Furthermore, we propose an extension of SIQHDy for scenarios with limited accessible observables and evaluate its performance in identifying three-spin systems and in network-structure identification for five-spin systems.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum circuit learning framework inspired by SINDy to sparsely identify quantum Hamiltonian dynamics from measurement time-series data.
motivation: Estimating the Hamiltonian of a quantum system from experimental data is crucial for characterizing and controlling quantum devices, but existing methods often require many measurements or prior knowledge.
method: The method represents the unitary evolution as a product of basis quantum circuits and uses sparsity-promoting optimization to estimate the circuit parameters from time-series data of measurement outcomes.
result: Numerical demonstrations show accurate reconstruction of single-, three-, and five-spin systems, robustness to noise, and successful extension to limited observables and network-structure identification.
conclusion: The proposed SIQHDy framework offers a promising data-driven approach for Hamiltonian identification, with potential applications in quantum system characterization and quantum network inference.

title: Pas-qfl: Personalized Ansatz Selection For Quantum Federated Learning Under Client Data Heterogeneity
abstract: ArXiv:2608.14995v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum federated learning (QFL) lets multiple quantum clients collaboratively train quantum neural networks (QNNs) without sharing private local data. However, existing QFL methods commonly assume that all clients use the same ansatz, overlooking how heterogeneous client data affects ansatz suitability. Under class-imbalanced non-IID data, different clients may favor different ansatz structures, so a fixed ansatz can lead to unstable and unfair performance across clients. In this paper, we propose PAS-QFL, a Personalized Ansatz Selection framework for QFL under client data heterogeneity. Rather than treating the ansatz as a monolithic structure, PAS-QFL decomposes each client QNN into a globally shared ansatz and a client-specific private ansatz, and personalizes the structure of the private ansatz rather than only its parameters. The shared ansatz is placed first and selected by a stability-aware cross-client criterion so that its parameters can be reliably aggregated, while the private ansatz serves as a personalized decision head, selected per client by local Macro-F1 to adapt the shared representation to its local data. During training, each client updates both its shared and private parameters locally but uploads only the shared parameters, so federated aggregation stays well-defined while each client keeps its own private structure. PAS-QFL uses Macro-F1 as the primary selection metric to avoid misleading accuracy under class imbalance. Experiments on heterogeneous QFL tasks show that PAS-QFL improves average Macro-F1 over the existing fixed-ansatz QFL baselines, demonstrating the value of personalizing the ansatz structure for practical QFL.
tldr: This paper proposes a personalized ansatz selection framework for quantum federated learning to handle client data heterogeneity.
motivation: Existing QFL methods assume a fixed ansatz for all clients, which can lead to unstable and unfair performance under non-IID data.
method: PAS-QFL decomposes each client's QNN into a shared ansatz and a client-specific private ansatz, selecting the shared ansatz via a stability-aware criterion and the private ansatz per client using local Macro-F1.
result: Experiments show that PAS-QFL improves average Macro-F1 over fixed-ansatz QFL baselines on heterogeneous tasks.
conclusion: Personalizing the ansatz structure is valuable for practical QFL under data heterogeneity.
